About Nabla

Nabla delivers a unified clinical AI platform used by healthcare organizations across specialties and care settings. The platform includes:

Ambient AI documentation that captures clinical conversations and generates structured notes.

AI-powered dictation and clinical workflow tools embedded directly within EHR systems.

Agentic AI capabilities that support multi-step clinical and administrative tasks.

Enterprise-grade infrastructure built for secure deployment across health systems.

The best of AI at the service of healthcare

Nabla’s phenomenal traction is the result of 3 years of diligent product development.

Led by former Meta AI Research engineers, our team has consistently anticipated how AI can revolutionize healthcare delivery. Our Machine Learning team continually leverages the latest advancements to unlock AI’s full potential in healthcare.

Yann LeCun, Meta’s ex-Chief AI Scientist and Turing award winner, is an advisor to Nabla. He’s now focused on AMI Labs, with whom we have a close partnership.

Engineering at Nabla

Engineering at Nabla is lean, fast-moving, and deeply technical. Our teams span machine learning, native desktop applications, and platform infrastructure to deliver AI into clinical settings reliably and at scale.

Your team

At Nabla, product development is led jointly by Engineering and Product and organized into cross-functional squads, each focused on a specific product area. Squads bring together product managers, designers, engineers of different profiles, and domain experts, and operate with a high level of ownership.

As a Full-stack Engineer, you'll join one of these squads and contribute end to end to a specific part of the product.

The technical challenges

  • Volumetry and efficiency: We handle more than 2.5 million medical encounters per month. Each one is automatically turned into a clinical note sent to the clinician's patient record system, saving thousands of hours of administrative work and giving healthcare professionals more time for their patients.

  • Real-time audio transcription: capturing and streaming audio reliably, from in-person visits as well as video consultations, and turning it into transcripts with very low latency

  • Resilience: keeping the product working on weak or unstable networks, with no data lost and no disruption to the clinician

  • Healthcare integrations: building robust connections to the third-party medical systems clinicians already rely on.

  • Complex AI services: designing and running multi-stage LLM pipelines and agentic workflows at scale, with the reliability and auditability a clinical setting requires

These challenges come with demanding product requirements:

  • Zero friction: clinicians have no time to learn a new tool, so the product must be fast to set up, intuitive, and useful from the very first consultation

  • Trust: what we generate goes into patient records, so quality and reliability are non-negotiable

  • Works everywhere: web, desktop and mobile, in clinics, hospitals or remote consultations

  • Build and improve product features across web, desktop and mobile platforms

  • Design and evolve the back-end APIs and services that power them

  • Collaborate closely with Product, ML, and Design to take projects from idea to production

requirements and performance.

🚀 Already more than 900,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and over 6000 accounting firms use Pennylane in France!

Your impact

Great growth decisions start with reliable data.

At Pennylane, we're building the financial operating system for European businesses. As we grow and expand into new markets, understanding how users discover, interact with and adopt our product is becoming increasingly important.

That's where Growth Engineering comes in.

We're looking for a Growth Engineer with strong data and tracking expertise to help us build reliable, scalable tracking and analytics foundations across our digital acquisition journeys.

You'll join our Growth Engineering team and work closely with Thomas, our Growth Engineering Team Lead, within the Marketing Website squad.

Your mission ? Make sure we collect the right data, trust what we measure and turn insights into better growth decisions.

What you'll do

Build reliable tracking foundations

You'll own the technical implementation and reliability of tracking across our website and acquisition funnels.

  • Design, implement and maintain tracking plans across key user journeys.

  • Build and improve event tracking, user identification and data collection.

  • Work with tools such as Segment, Amplitude and Google Tag Manager.

  • Ensure tracking consistency, accuracy and reliability across our digital ecosystem.

  • Identify and resolve tracking issues before they impact business decisions.

Connect data across our growth ecosystem

You'll help build the technical connections between our website, internal systems and analytics tools.

  • Develop and maintain APIs and integrations between platforms.

  • Ensure reliable data flows between our acquisition, product and analytics tools.

  • Collaborate with Data teams to improve data quality and consistency.

  • Support the evolution of our tracking architecture as Pennylane scales internationally.

Power experimentation and conversion

You'll work closely with Growth, Marketing and Data teams to understand user behavior and improve acquisition performance.

  • Implement the technical foundations for A/B testing and experimentation.

  • Help measure acquisition funnels and identify opportunities for improvement.

  • Ensure experiments are properly tracked and measurable.

  • Translate business questions into clear technical tracking requirements.

  • Support data-driven decisions through reliable instrumentation.

Contribute as an engineer

This is an engineering role, not a reporting or dashboarding position.

You'll be expected to bring strong technical fundamentals and take ownership of your work.

  • Write clean, maintainable and well-tested code.

  • Build scalable and reliable technical solutions.

  • Investigate complex tracking and data issues.

  • Improve existing systems, processes and documentation.

  • Collaborate with engineers across Growth, Engineering and Data teams.

  • Contribute to technical decisions and engineering best practices.

Who are you?

We're looking for an engineer who understands both how data is collected and why it matters.

Someone who enjoys solving technical problems, working with different teams and making sure that business decisions are based on data people can trust.

You don't need to be a data scientist or a marketing specialist. But you should be comfortable working at the intersection of software engineering, analytics and growth.

We'd love to meet you if...

  • You have a software engineering experience, with hands-on exposure to tracking, analytics or data integrations.

  • You have implemented and maintained event tracking across websites, applications or acquisition funnels.

  • You're fluent in AI-assisted development : you work with coding agents, create custom skills and instructions, use worktrees to parallelize work and keep code quality high.

  • You're familiar with tools such as Segment, Amplitude, Google Tag Manager or similar platforms.

  • You understand event schemas, data layers, user identification and tracking consistency.

  • You're comfortable working with JavaScript and APIs to implement and troubleshoot tracking.

  • You care about code quality, reliability and maintainability.

  • You enjoy taking ownership of technical projects, from design to production.

  • You're comfortable working in French and English.

Bonus points if you have experience with:

  • Ruby on Rails, Vue.js or Nuxt.js.

  • SQL and data warehouses.

  • Server-side tracking and conversion APIs.

  • A/B testing and experimentation platforms.

  • Attribution, conversion measurement or acquisition analytics.

  • Privacy-conscious tracking and consent management.

  • International websites and multi-market acquisition funnels.

Qui sommes-nous ?
column2: Q ENERGY France est un acteur majeur du marché des énergies renouvelables en France. Autrefois affilié au groupe RES, l’entreprise œuvre depuis 27 ans dans le développement, la construction et l’exploitation de projets éoliens et photovoltaïques.
column5: Aujourd'hui également positionnée sur le marché du stockage d'énergie, Q ENERGY poursuit son expansion vers de nouveaux domaines afin de proposer des solutions intelligentes et complètes pour la production et la fourniture d’énergie durable en France.
column7: L'entreprise compte près de 300 collaborateur.rice.s et 6 agences sur le territoire ainsi qu'un siège social basé à Avignon. Q ENERGY France est une entreprise de la holding européenne Q ENERGY Solutions, créée en 2021 par Hanwha Solutions dans l'objectif de conduire à la prochaine génération de production d'énergie verte et flexible en Europe. Basée à Berlin, Q ENERGY Solutions est une société sœur de Q CELLS, fabricant de modules photovoltaïques reconnu à travers le monde. Les deux sociétés constituent la division Energie du groupe Hanwha Solutions, basé à Séoul.
column10: Vous serez support au pilotage et à l'animation d'études d'impacts sur l'environnement de parcs éoliens et centrales solaires comprenant notamment le volet naturel, le volet paysager et des études spécifiques.

column13: Vous participerez à la concertation de tous les acteurs permettant de réaliser la conception de projets la plus adaptée au territoire.

Op duizenden werkvloeren in Nederland wordt dagelijks gewerkt met gevaarlijke stoffen. Dat kan veilig, als je weet wat je in huis hebt, wat het doet en welke regels erbij horen. Daar helpt Sdu Toxic organisaties bij. Toxic is de meest complete SaaS-oplossing voor wet- en regelgeving rond gevaarlijke stoffen in Nederland. Organisaties registreren er hun stoffen mee, beoordelen blootstelling, leggen maatregelen vast en informeren hun medewerkers. Zo helpen we QHSE-professionals om mensen veilig te laten werken en aan de arbowetgeving te voldoen. Achter Toxic staat een team met diepgaande kennis van chemische producten en de regels die erbij horen. En een succesvol marketing- en salesteam dat zorgt dat steeds meer organisaties ons vinden.
column3:
>

Toxic is onderdeel van Lefebvre Sdu, dat al 200 jaar bouwt aan juridische en fiscale kennis, en van Lefebvre Group, de Europese leider op dat gebied. De vraag groeit. Onze Commercieel Medewerkers Binnendienst en marketing plannen meer afspraken in dan we nu kunnen afronden. Daarom zoeken we een Senior Accountmanager die van die gesprekken klanten maakt.
column4:
>

HOE JIJ ONS VERDER BRENGT

Jij bent het gezicht van Toxic. Voor de veiligheidskundigen, managers en directies die met ons werken, word jij degene die ze kennen en vertrouwen. Je leert hun organisatie kennen, luistert naar wat er speelt en denkt mee over wat ze nodig hebben. Zo bouw je relaties die jaren meegaan, en groeit Toxic met je klanten mee.

  • Je leert je klanten kennen: hun mensen, hun processen en wat er bij hen speelt. Zo word je hun vaste gesprekspartner en denk je mee over de volgende stap.

  • Elke nieuwe relatie begint met een goed gesprek. De binnendienst en marketing plannen de afspraken, jij bereidt je voor en ontdekt wat een organisatie nodig heeft. Daarnaast zoek je zelf nieuwe kansen.

  • In je demo's laat je zien hoe Toxic werkt en wat het oplevert. Gaat de vraag verder dan het standaardplatform? Dan werk je met collega's een oplossing op maat uit, met API-koppelingen en AI-toepassingen.

  • Je bouwt relaties met veiligheidskundigen, inkopers en directie, brengt hun belangen samen in 1 voorstel en sluit deals met een hogere dealwaarde.

  • Met strategische accountplannen houd je overzicht op je belangrijkste klanten. Je ziet kansen voor up- en cross-sell en herkent retentierisico's vroeg. Samen met Customer Success zorg je dat nieuwe klanten goed starten.

  • Je houdt je pipeline en forecast actueel in Salesforce en deelt wat je bij klanten hoort met marketing en product.

  • Als senior ben je mentor en sparringpartner voor collega-accountmanagers.


DIT ZOEKEN WIJ

Je bent iemand bij wie klanten zich gehoord voelen. Je luistert goed, stelt de juiste vragen en vertaalt een complex vraagstuk naar een helder voorstel. De markt van gevaarlijke stoffen hoef je nog niet te kennen. Wat je wel meebrengt, is ervaring met het opbouwen van klantrelaties en interesse in software.

  • Je hebt meerdere jaren ervaring als accountmanager, bij voorkeur in SaaS of met digitale oplossingen.

  • Je hebt interesse in software en wilt begrijpen hoe een platform als Toxic werkt, inclusief API-koppelingen en AI-toepassingen.

  • Je bouwt relaties met meerdere stakeholders tegelijk en beheerst het volledige salesproces, van eerste kennismaking tot getekend contract.

  • Je stuurt op data en haalt je targets, met nieuwe klanten en binnen je eigen portefeuille.

  • Je spreekt en schrijft vloeiend Nederlands.

  • Je hoeft de markt nog niet te kennen. Klanten, stoffen en regelgeving leer je bij ons, van collega's die het vak door en door kennen.
column5:
>

TomTom's map is seen by millions of people every day - in dashboards, on phones, and across partner products worldwide. As a Senior UX Designer on the Map Visualisation team, you will shape how our 2D and 3D geospatial data is designed, styled and delivered across TomTom's product portfolio.

You'll spend your days crafting multi-zoom map experiences, working with spatial data and collaborating closely with engineers and product managers to turn cartographic intent into production-ready map styles. You'll need to be as comfortable discussing label collision and style-layer specifications with engineers as you are refining colour palettes and visual hierarchy.

This is a product role first. You'll be embedded in a cross-functional team that ships map rendering, map styles and SDKs used by other TomTom products and by the customers who build on our platform. You'll take part in the whole development lifecycle, from discovery and solution design through pull requests to release. Your product judgement, and your ability to bring people with competing priorities to a clear decision, matter here as much as your cartographic craft.

AI is part of how we work. We expect you to use it to explore, prototype and ship faster, to know where it falls short, and to help shape map experiences in products where AI is part of the experience itself.

Design Compelling Map Experiences Create and refine 2D and 3D map visualisations from concept through production delivery. Own the end-to-end cartographic design process - from data exploration and sketching through to style implementation, QA and iteration across zoom levels, regions and use cases.

Maintain and Evolve Core Map Styles Enhance TomTom's core map styles, ensuring consistency, readability and visual quality across platforms, screen densities and global markets. Balance aesthetic ambition with rendering performance and data constraints.

Work as Part of the Product Team Work day-to-day alongside software engineers and product managers building TomTom's map data structures, renderers and SDKs. Take part in planning, refinement and reviews, provide design specifications engineers can act on, and review visual output during development and before release.

Make and Own Trade-offs Help decide what ships, when and at what quality. Weigh visual fidelity against render budget, memory and frame rate on automotive and mobile hardware, customer requests against platform consistency, and scope against release dates. Reach a decision with the people who own the product, record it and see it through.

Contribute to Renderer and Tooling Requirements Provide detailed input on the data and rendering capabilities needed to achieve design goals. Define requirements for internal cartographic authoring tools and identify workflow improvements that raise the team's output quality and speed.

Bring AI into the Design Workflow Use AI to shorten the loop from idea to rendered map: generating and editing style-spec JSON, scripting data exploration, and building interactive prototypes on real data instead of static frames. Turn what works into shared workflows the team can reuse, and help define how we check AI-generated output for cartographic quality.

Design for AI-Driven Map Experiences Contribute to how the map responds when the request comes from an AI system rather than a tap, for example in GeoAI answers, conversational search or agent-generated routes. Work out how the map shows what the AI found, how confident it is and when it is wrong.

Inform Decisions with Research and Data Participate in user research, customer conversations and competitive benchmarking. Use insights to ground design decisions and advocate for improvements that address real user needs.

Support the Design System and Standards Contribute to the Map Visualisation design system - documenting patterns, conventions and cartographic guidelines that enable consistency and scale across the product portfolio.
A track record of shaping product direction from the design seat. You set out the options, make the case for one and bring engineering, product and business stakeholders with you.

A track record of shipping software as a designer embedded in a product team, ideally on map, location or developer-platform products: SDKs, APIs, map styles or tooling that other teams and companies build on.

A clear understanding of how products move from discovery to release and beyond, including planning, roadmaps and measuring results after launch. You know how versioned releases, deprecations and backwards compatibility shape design choices on a platform with external customers.

Hands-on familiarity with how software gets built: backlogs, refinement, estimation, definition of done, Git, pull requests, code reviews, CI/CD, feature flags and release trains. You don't need to write production code, but you need to understand how your designs move through a rendering pipeline and into a release.
Sound judgement under constraint. You can point to decisions where you gave something up to ship, and explain why it was right for the product and its users.
Clarity with senior audiences. You can turn a complex design problem into a short, well-argued recommendation and own the result.
Comfort with disagreement. You challenge a decision with evidence, accept the outcome when it goes the other way and keep the work moving.
Experience contributing to solution design documents, technical specifications and cross-functional planning.

A solid foundation in digital cartography, GIS or geographic information design. If your map-making depth is still growing, show us how fast you are closing the gap, including how you use AI to learn.
Experience designing multi-zoom digital maps with attention to cartographic conventions, label placement, generalisation and cultural adaptation.
Working proficiency with key mapping technologies and ecosystems: MapLibre, Mapbox GL JS, OpenStreetMap data and tooling, QGIS, ArcGIS, Leaflet, OpenLayers or comparable platforms.
Experience working with diverse spatial datasets - vector tiles, raster tiles, GeoJSON, shapefiles, point clouds or terrain data.
Awareness of cartographic standards across regions and cultures, including sensitive topics such as disputed borders and local place names.
Demonstrated ability to build visually compelling 2D and 3D map experiences - from thematic styling and terrain visualisation to street-level detail.

Hands-on experience designing 3D map content such as buildings, terrain, landmarks and lane-level road geometry, in stylised or realistic form. You understand how LOD, lighting, materials and camera pitch affect legibility and performance.
Experience with 3D data formats and pipelines such as glTF and 3D Tiles, and how 3D assets are prepared and optimised for real-time map rendering.
Good understanding of real-time rendering concepts as they apply to maps: style layers, zoom interpolation, data-driven styling, symbol rendering and performance considerations.
Evidence that AI has changed how you work. Be ready to show a real example, such as a map style, data visualisation or coded prototype built with AI, and tell us where it let you down.
Sharp judgement of AI output. You can spot errors in generated work and know which decisions still need a designer's eye.
Experience turning personal AI use into workflows the team shares, within the limits of confidential data and licensing.
5+ years of professional experience in UX, product or cartographic design, with most of that time spent inside software product teams.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Cartography, Geography, GIS, UX Design, Computer Science or a related field - or equivalent professional experience.
Ability to build clear, concise prototypes and specification documentation that bridge design and engineering.
Strong visual and graphic design fundamentals - typography, colour theory, hierarchy and layout.
User-centric mindset with a collaborative, low-ego approach to problem-solving.
High attention to detail and a real passion for the craft of map making.
Experience with game engines or 3D content pipelines (Unity, Unreal Engine, Blender) and their application to geospatial visualisation.

Familiarity with front-end languages and graphics APIs (JavaScript/TypeScript, WebGL, WebGPU, GLSL) or scripting for cartographic automation (Python, PostGIS, Overpass API). With AI, even basic coding skills go a long way.
Experience with map data processing tools and pipelines: Tippecanoe, Tilemaker, osm2pgsql, Mapnik or similar.
Understanding of the automotive, fleet management or logistics industries and their mapping requirements.
Familiarity with emerging trends in spatial computing, AR navigation or digital twins.
Experience contributing to design systems at scale.

column1: We are deliberately not splitting data engineering from analytics. At our size the hard problems sit in the handover between the two, and we want one person who enjoys that whole puzzle.

The team serves four groups with genuinely different needs. Growth wants hourly to daily signals and can live with approximately right. Carrier reporting and corporate finance are calendar-locked and need numbers that reconcile and survive an audit months later. Actuarial needs depth and lineage over speed. Prioritising here is arbitration between things that fail in different ways, and the arbitration is yours.

It's a hands-on role. You can open the warehouse and read the models, you review a new data model before it ships, and your team trusts your technical judgement because you still use it. The job is still the team: its own game, its communication, and each person in it. When something slips, hands-on work is the first thing that yields.

• Owning the trade-offs between Growth, carrier reporting, finance and actuarial: deciding what the team works on, driving alignment with key partners across other teams, and saying no when the answer is no

• Making the platform scale: a new country, carrier or product should mean configuration and reused models, and recurring manual work, like carrier reporting and cash reconciliation, should turn into automation
• Bringing engineering excellence to how the team works: data contracts with product teams, testing in CI, alerts that get resolved, a way to try changes before they hit production

About Us:

Tebi is creating the first Connected Restaurant Management System that makes hospitality flow. In one seamless platform, Tebi embeds sales, reservations, kitchen prep, payments, and all the data that powers it, creating smooth service and intuitive insights.
Founded by Arnout Schuijff, co-founder of Adyen, and backed by €50 million in funding from Index Ventures &
column2: CapitalG, Tebi is built in service of hospitality first. Thousands of restaurants, cafés, bars, and coffee shops across the Netherlands, UK, Italy, Spain, Germany, Denmark and Finland already love running on Tebi.
column4:

About the role:

We’re looking for a Senior AI Engineer to build and run the agents at the heart of Tebi OS. You’ll design, ship, evaluate and scale our Product Agents, along with the data pipelines, tools and infrastructure that make them reliable in production.

The ideal candidate started in data or ML engineering and has since moved into AI engineering, building LLM-powered agents for real users. You enjoy turning messy financial and operational data into context an agent can reason over and act on with confidence and you are passionate about solving product challenges through AI.

You’ll work closely with product and engineering to put intelligence into the hands of hospitality teams. That could be an agent that answers questions about a restaurant’s finances in real time, one that automates repetitive back-office tasks, or internal tools that help us move faster.

What you’ll do:

  • Design, build and operate production agents: orchestration, tool and function calling, memory, multi-step reasoning, and integration with Tebi’s backend services

  • Build the data foundations agents rely on, including real-time and batch pipelines over financial and operational data, retrieval layers, and well-modeled datasets agents can query safely and accurately

  • Turn APIs and internal services into well-defined agent tools, and own the contracts between agents and the rest of the platform

  • Set up evaluation for agent behavior: offline eval sets, LLM-as-judge and human review, regression testing on prompt and model changes, and feedback loops that improve agents over time

  • Own observability for agents in production by tracing sessions, tool calls and model calls, and tracking latency, cost, error rates and quality

  • Work with product teams to find where agents can meaningfully improve the customer experience or internal workflows, and say clearly where they can’t

  • Make sure agents handle data securely and responsibly, with sensible guardrails, access controls, and protection against prompt injection and data leakage

What you’ll bring:

  • 7+ years in software engineering, with a solid base in data or ML engineering

  • Hands-on experience building and shipping LLM agents to production, not just prototypes. You’ve dealt with flaky tool calls, runaway loops, hallucinated arguments and token budgets, and you have opinions on how to handle them.

  • Strong data modeling and data warehousing fundamentals, plus experience with ingestion, transformation and data quality

  • Strong SQL, and experience with pipeline tools (e.g. Airflow, dbt) and analytical or cloud data platforms (e.g. ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake)

  • Experience evaluating and monitoring LLM systems, and an understanding of the full lifecycle from experiment to deployment to ongoing improvement

  • Backend engineering skills: you’re comfortable building the API endpoint that exposes an agent’s output to the frontend, or the service an agent calls as a tool

  • Clear communication, including the ability to explain trade-offs in latency, cost, accuracy and complexity to product partners

  • A product mindset. You care about how your work lands with users, and you’re keen to meet customers face to face to understand their needs.

This probably isn't the role for you if you have been working with AI agents to improve your day to day working flows but you haven’t built an Agent in the production.

People who succeed at Tebi are independent, curious and passionate about hospitality. If this speaks to you we can be the right fit. Learn more about how we work from our Recipe here: https://www.tebi.com/gb/careers .

Benefits:

  • Start-up Equity

  • Competitive Salary

  • Lunch Provided in Office

  • Team building events

  • Unlimited time off

What is Restaurant Software?

Restaurants and other merchants use various software systems such as Point of Sale (POS), Reservations, Kitchen Display Systems (KDS), Payments, Inventory, Staffing, and the list goes on. These systems all need to speak to each other which they frequently don’t. It’s a mess, and we are fixing it.

From buying a croissant at a cafe to having dinner with friends, it’s a €4 Trillion+ global market and a critical part of everyday life in today's economy.

How we use AI at Tebi

We use AI the way our merchants use Tebi, to cut out the friction and get to what matters faster. We believe in a world where AI increases quality, efficiency and speed.

At Tebi, AI isn't a policy or a checkbox, it's just part of how we work. It helps us write, analyse, build, and improve but doesn’t make the last call. If there's a smarter way to do something, we want to find it.

Omschrijving

Wij zijn voor de Gemeente Zwolle op zoek naar een Senior Financieel Strategisch Adviseur. Binnen de afdeling Concernstaf werk je aan een strategische en impactvolle opgave: het ontwikkelen van een integraal Meerjarig Investeringsplan (MIP) met een horizon van tien jaar en een bijbehorend financieel sturingskader.

De gemeente staat de komende jaren voor grote investeringen op het gebied van woningbouw, gebiedsontwikkeling, onderwijshuisvesting en infrastructuur. Tegelijkertijd vragen financiële schaarste, beperkte uitvoeringscapaciteit en netcongestie om scherpe keuzes en integrale afwegingen. In deze opdracht zorg je voor een toekomstbestendige financiële aanpak die inzicht geeft in investeringen, risico’s, financiële consequenties en prioriteiten binnen de gemeentelijke investeringsportefeuille.

Deze interim opdracht is interessant voor een ervaren strategisch financieel adviseur met ruime ervaring binnen gemeentelijke organisaties, financiële sturing en investeringsvraagstukken in het fysieke domein.

  • Je ontwikkelt en implementeert een integraal Meerjarig Investeringsplan (MIP) met een looptijd van tien jaar.

  • Je ontwikkelt een financieel sturingskader voor gemeentelijke investeringen, inclusief financiële uitgangspunten en besluitvormingscriteria.

  • Je ontwikkelt een methodiek voor integrale prioritering van investeringsprojecten op basis van financiële, bestuurlijke en organisatorische factoren.

  • Je adviseert over de aansluiting van het MIP en het sturingskader op de planning- en controlcyclus (P&

Distribusion is the world’s leading ground transportation marketplace and gives travellers seamless access to ground transportation online, from search to ticket purchase. We have built a cutting-edge B2B technology platform that connects bus, rail and ferry operators in 70+ countries with the biggest online retailers including Google Maps and Booking.com.
column2:

We are shaping the future of travel and building the largest global network of transport providers and retailers. We are one of the fastest growing startups in travel, backed by leading venture capital investors including TQ Ventures, Lightrock, Creandum, and Northzone, and are headquartered in Berlin, Germany. Following our recent $80m Series C funding, we are ready to push beyond.
column3:
>

We are looking for an experienced Senior Penetration Tester to join us on a 6-month contract, and start as soon as possible. You will run hands-on, authenticated security testing across a real attack surface: public partner-facing booking APIs, payment flows, web and mobile apps used by millions of travellers, and the cloud infrastructure behind them. You’ll plan and run your own testing, work directly with our engineering squads to get findings fixed, and see your impact in production within weeks.
column4:
>

What you will do:

  • Test our partner-facing booking APIs against the OWASP API Security Top 10, with a focus on object- and function-level authorization, tenant isolation, mass assignment, data exposure and rate limiting.

  • Assess API authentication and integrity end to end, including OAuth 2.0/OIDC, API keys, JWTs, webhooks and request signing.

  • Hunt for business-logic abuse in booking, checkout, payment and refund flows, including race conditions and pricing manipulation.

  • Run authenticated tests of traveller-, partner- and operator-facing web and mobile apps following OWASP WSTG and ASVS, including how passenger personal data is stored, shown and exported.

  • Review cloud, Kubernetes and CI/CD configurations and secrets handling for attack paths that could be chained from an application bug.

  • Map and regularly test our internet-facing attack surface.

  • Red-team our AI features (assistants, agents, support bots) against the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.

  • Write clear, reproducible, risk-rated findings with practical remediation guidance, walk engineers through fixes and verify them with retests.

Workplace:

We are a remote-first company with teams located around the Globe and a HQ in Berlin.



Who you are:

  • You bring 5+ years of hands-on penetration testing, mainly of web applications and APIs, and can point to recent engagements you’ve led end to end.

  • You have deep, practical knowledge of the OWASP API Security Top 10, WSTG and ASVS, including authentication/authorization models (OAuth2/OIDC, JWT), IDOR/BOLA, mass assignment, SSRF, injection and XSS.

  • You have found business-logic and race-condition vulnerabilities in transactional systems such as booking, e-commerce, payments or fintech.

  • You are fluent with Burp Suite Pro (or similar) and write your own scripts and tooling (Python, Go or similar).

  • You are comfortable assessing cloud and container environments (GCP preferred, Kubernetes) and CI/CD pipelines.

  • You work independently: you scope, prioritise, test and report with minimal guidance, and you explain complex risks plainly to engineers and leadership.

  • You are available to start at short notice.

  • Bonus Points: OSCP, OSWE, BSCP or similar certifications

founders-associate-intern-ai-product-consultant-munich-249672,qado GmbH,Founders Associate Intern: AI Product Consultant (m/w/d),"

Wir bauen die AI-Plattform für den Einkauf.

Der Einkauf verantwortet den größten Kostenblock in Unternehmen und sucht mit Tools von gestern in verstreuten Datensystemen nach Einsparungen. Der steigende Kostendruck zwingt CPOs, das zu ändern.

Unsere integrierten AI-Agents führen eigenständig Verhandlungen, sorgen dafür, dass vertraglich vereinbarte Einsparungen tatsächlich im Ergebnis ankommen, und bringen Intelligenz in langweilige, manuelle Aufgaben.

Wir scheuen uns nicht vor komplexen Daten und schaffen Intelligenz, die die Ökonomie des Einkaufs verändert, weit über einfache agentische Workflows hinaus.

Wir sind von Top-VCs (10x und Plug and Play) und Business Angels finanziert, und unsere Gründer bringen Erfahrung aus der Strategieberatung und aus schnell wachsenden Startups mit.

Wir sind drei Freunde, die sich seit Jahren kennen. Wir haben Spaß, bewegen uns schnell und uns geht es um echte Ergebnisse.

Aufgaben

Du bist Allrounder:in: technisch versiert, stark im Kundenkontakt und voller Energie, auch wenn du fünfmal am Tag das Thema wechselst. In der einen Stunde sitzt du einem CPO gegenüber und sorgst dafür, dass unsere AI überzeugt. In der nächsten steckst du im Produkt, findest heraus, warum ein Agent nicht geliefert hat, und gestaltest die Lösung mit.

Du willst aus einer ""interessanten AI-Demo"" einen unterschriebenen Enterprise-Vertrag mit nachgewiesenem Mehrwert machen, und du lässt nicht zu, dass gute Ideen zwischen Kunden und Techies verloren gehen. Das ist eine Founders-Associate-Rolle im wahrsten Sinne: Du arbeitest Seite an Seite mit den Gründern, verantwortest Kunden und Produkt, erlebst aus erster Reihe, wie ein Enterprise-AI-Unternehmen aufgebaut wird, und übernimmst vom ersten Tag an echte Verantwortung für Produkt und Kundenbeziehungen. Du lernst direkt von Gründern, die schon Unternehmen aufgebaut und skaliert haben.

Die Stelle ist nur als Praktikum in Vollzeit möglich, mit Start im April 2027 und einer Dauer von idealerweise 6 Monaten.

Du arbeitest an der Schnittstelle von Produkt, Vertrieb und Kunde, direkt mit den Gründern. Konkret:

  • Baue Demos, bei denen CPOs aufhorchen. Du entwickelst präzise, maßgeschneiderte Demos, die die Fähigkeiten unserer Agents in ein klares ""Das brauchen wir"" übersetzen, aufgebaut auf den echten Daten und echten Problemen des Interessenten statt auf einem generischen Durchklicken.

  • Bring Proof of Values zum Erfolg. Du begleitest den POV vom Kickoff bis zum Ergebnis: Du definierst vorab, was ""Erfolg"" bedeutet, hältst den Kunden engagiert, findest heraus, was nicht funktioniert, und lieferst einen Business Case, den der Kunde intern vertreten kann.

  • Verantworte Product Discovery von Anfang bis Ende. Du bereitest Kundeninterviews vor, um herauszufinden, was Einkaufsteams wirklich brauchen, analysierst den Wettbewerb, damit wir genau wissen, wo wir gewinnen, und übersetzt beides in klare Feature-Anforderungen für das Tech-Team.

  • Finde heraus, wo unsere Kunden hängen bleiben. Mit modernen Product-Management-Methoden erkennst du, wo Kunden aktuell auf Engpässe stoßen, und schreibst Briefings, damit unsere Engineers sie beheben.

Qualifikation

DEINE MISSION

Lust, Ernährung neu zu denken? Bei yfood machen wir seit 2017 gutes Essen alltagstauglich – ausgewogen, praktisch und richtig lecker. Mit unseren Produkten haben wir eine eigene Kategorie geformt: Smart Food. In ganz Europa unterwegs, rasant wachsend und immer auf der Suche nach neuen Ideen. Wenn du Teil eines dynamischen Teams sein möchtest, das die Lebensmittelbranche revolutioniert, dann bist du bei yfood genau richtig.

Du postest eh schon jeden Tag. Mach daraus deinen Job.
Du scrollst nicht nur – du weißt, warum ein Video durch die Decke geht und warum das nächste floppt. Genau dieses Gespür suchen wir. Der Großteil unserer Reichweite entsteht über Creator, nicht über uns selbst – und weil du selbst postest, sprichst du ihre Sprache und zeigst auf unseren eigenen Kanälen das Beste davon.
Die Rolle ist global gedacht: Du denkst unsere Social-Strategie nicht nur für DACH, sondern sparrst dich dabei auch mit unseren internationalen Marketing Leads, zum Beispiel dem Head of Marketing in UK.
Die Position ist zunächst als Elternzeitvertretung auf zwei Jahre befristet.

• Strategie, global gedacht: Du entwickelst unsere Social Media Strategie nicht im stillen Kämmerlein in München, sondern im Austausch mit unseren internationalen Marketing Leads. Du hinterfragst HQ-Vorgaben, wenn UK oder ein anderer Markt etwas anderes braucht, und sorgst dafür, dass Strategie und lokale Realität zusammenpassen.

• TikTok ist dein zweites Zuhause: Du erkennst Trends, bevor sie durch sind, und weißt sofort, welche Formate zu yfood passen und welche nicht. Instagram und YouTube bespielst du mit, aber TikTok ist dein Hauptrevier.
• Deine eigenen Kanäle, dein Anspruch: Du verantwortest unsere DACH-Kanäle und zeigst dort die stärksten Creator Videos, Produktlaunches und informativen Content. Qualität vor Quantität.

• Du sprichst Creator-Sprache: Weil du selbst Content machst, schreibst du Briefings, die Raum für eigene Ideen lassen, und gibst Feedback, das Creator tatsächlich weiterbringt, statt sie nur zufriedenzustellen.
• Du machst Markenmomente viral: Große Produktlaunches, außergewöhnliche Events und Creator Kampagnen bringst du auf Social und bist dabei auch in den Kommentaren mittendrin statt nur Beobachter.
• Daten sind dein Vibe-Check: Du planst im Redaktionskalender, schaust auf Watch Time, Saves, Shares und Hook Rate und machst konsequent mehr von dem, was funktioniert.

• Kein Soloprojekt: Du arbeitest eng mit Content & Comms, Influencer & Creator, Creative, Brand Activation, Performance und E-Commerce zusammen. Social ist bei uns nicht einfach nur ein Kanal, sondern das Betriebssystem.
• Du bist selbst Social: Aktiv auf TikTok, idealerweise mit eigenem Content – zeig uns gern deinen Kanal. Instagram und YouTube kennst du ebenfalls aus dem Effeff.
• 2+ Jahre Erfahrung im Social Media Marketing – ob Brand, Agentur, Start-up oder als Creator. Food, FMCG oder Lifestyle sind ein Plus, kein Muss.
• Plattform-Fluency: Sounds, Duett/Stitch, Green Screen, Reels, Carousels, Shorts – du weißt aus eigener Erfahrung, was wo funktioniert und warum.
• Creator-Verständnis: Du weißt, wie Creator ticken, und formulierst Briefings und Feedback so, dass sie auch ankommen.
• Analyse mit Attitüde: Watch Time, Saves, Shares, Hook-Rate sind für dich Steuerrad, kein Selbstzweck.
Wir sind ein bisschen anders – und genau das macht uns aus
• Leidenschaft – Wir brennen für das, was wir tun. Voller Energie, voller Optimismus, immer hungrig nach Neuem.
• Verantwortung – Heißt für uns: Füreinander einstehen, Verantwortung übernehmen und alles geben, wenn’s drauf ankommt.
• Professionalität – Wir nehmen unsere Arbeit ernst – uns selbst aber nicht zu sehr. Wir sind offen, direkt und immer auf Augenhöhe. Kein Bullshit, kein Ego. Nur Team.
• Innovation – Wir denken lieber „Warum eigentlich nicht?“ statt „Das war schon immer so.“ Wir lieben neue Ideen, unkonventionelle Wege – und bleiben nie stehen.
• Wir fördern Chancengleichheit und schätzen Vielfalt. Wir verpflichten uns, ein integratives Umfeld für alle Mitarbeitende zu schaffen.

• yfood wächst international: Obwohl Deutschland unsers „Home Base“ ist, haben wir mit unseren internationalen Märkten ein dynamisches und buntes Umfeld geschaffen, in dem viele spannende Themen auf Dich warten.
• Agilität ist uns wichtig. Daher arbeiten wir in einem hybriden Arbeitsmodell und bieten dir die Möglichkeit mit Workation aus dem EU-Ausland zu arbeiten.
• Urlaub ist wichtig. Daher erhältst du bei uns 30 Tage bezahlten Urlaub im Jahr.

• yfood hält dich fit. Mit einer subventionierten Mitgliedschaft bei EGYM-Wellpass kannst du dir für nur 29€ im Monat Gutes tun. Dazu bieten wir im Rahmen unseres Gesundheitsmanagements & Healthy@yfood Workshops und Aktionen (z.B. Yoga, Breathwork, Soccer, Pickleball) an.
• Gemeinsam Gutes tun. Mit unserem yforgood Day erhältst du einen bezahlten Tag pro Jahr, um gemeinsam mit deinem Team eine soziale, gemeinnützige oder ökologische Initiative zu unterstützen.
• Weg vom Fleck. Wir steuern 30€ zu deinem ÖPNV-Ticket bei und bieten dir über JobRad die Möglichkeit, vergünstigt ein Fahrrad zu leasen.

• Trainiere deine Geschmacksnerven. Bei uns ist jeder der Lust hat Teil unseres Sensory-Teams. Probiere also neue Produkte, Sorten oder Geschmäcker vor allen anderen. Ansonsten gibt es so viel yfood wie du tragen kannst, natürlich auch für dich gratis.
• Als Start-Up hat man oft mit Klischees zu kämpfen. Manche sind aber auch wahr. Daher gibt es bei uns natürlich auch einen Obstkorb, deinen gratis Koffein-Kick oder das stille Wässerchen.
• Come as you are. Ob im Anzug oder Einhorn-Onesie. Einen Dresscode kennen wir nicht.

Promethion Industries is a European defence technology company building autonomous supremacy systems for aerial and multi-domain operations. We design tightly integrated autonomy stacks in Europe to enable decisive autonomy for NATO-aligned forces, focusing on defensive and counter-system capabilities including anti-UAS and resilient autonomy under contested conditions.

We are looking for a Senior Robotics Autonomy Engineer to build the intelligence that turns mission objectives, target information and vehicle state into executable autonomous behaviour.

Your mission with us

  • Build the autonomy layer of our high-speed aerial robotic systems.

  • Convert mission objectives, target state and vehicle state into real-time actions and trajectories.

  • Develop algorithms for dynamic rendezvous, pursuit, interception and terminal approach.

  • Build target-motion prediction and intercept-point estimation for moving airborne targets.

  • Develop real-time path planning, trajectory generation and replanning under uncertainty.

  • Account for aircraft capabilities, energy, maneuverability, sensing uncertainty and changing target behaviour.

  • Build decision and behaviour logic that allows the system to adapt continuously during a mission.

  • Combine classical robotics, optimization, MPC and learned approaches where appropriate.

  • Explore reinforcement learning, imitation learning and policy-based autonomy where they provide meaningful advantages.

  • Work closely with perception, estimation and control engineers to close the autonomy loop.

  • Take algorithms from simulation into real aircraft and validate them through repeated flight testing.

  • Strong robotics or autonomous-systems background with significant real-world deployment experience.

  • Strong experience with motion planning, trajectory generation or autonomous decision-making.

  • Deep understanding of kinematics, dynamics and optimization.

  • Experience with trajectory optimization, optimal control, MPC or comparable approaches.

  • Strong C++ skills and good Python skills.

  • Experience deploying autonomy algorithms onto real robotic systems.

  • Strong understanding of uncertainty and its implications for decision-making and planning.

  • Ability to design algorithms that operate under real-time compute constraints.

  • Hands-on attitude and willingness to participate directly in flight testing and system debugging.

Big plus

  • UAV / fixed-wing autonomy.

  • High-speed aerial robotics.

  • Rendezvous, pursuit or intercept problems.

  • Target-motion prediction.

  • Aggressive flight.

  • Reinforcement learning on real robots.

  • Imitation learning / learned policies.

  • PX4.

  • ROS2.

  • Optimal control and trajectory optimization.

  • Aviation, defence or space systems.

projektingenieur-entwicklung-teilprojektleitung-prototypen-und-pruftechnik-ostfildern-464576,Alveon MedTech GmbH,Projektingenieur Entwicklung (m/w/x) – Teilprojektleitung Prototypen und Prüftechnik,"

Die Alveon MedTech GmbH ist ein innovatives Medizintechnik-Startup mit Sitz in Ostfildern bei Stuttgart. Unser Fokus liegt auf der Entwicklung medizinischer Inhalationssysteme. Seit unserer Gründung im Jahr 2020 haben wir erfolgreich eine patentgeschützte Basistechnologie entwickelt. Aktuell arbeiten wir – im Rahmen einer strategischen Partnerschaft mit einem der größten deutschen Unternehmen im Medizinalcannabis-Markt – an der Entwicklung und Zulassung des ersten dosierfähigen Cannabis-Inhalators für den europäischen Markt.

Jetzt steht die entscheidende Phase an: Prototypen, Versuche, Verifikation und Zulassung. Dafür erweitern wir unsere Prüfkapazitäten in Ostfildern und bei externen Partnern und suchen jemanden, der diesen Bereich verantwortet.

Als Projektingenieur Entwicklung und Prüftechnik übernimmst du abgegrenzte Entwicklungsbereiche mit voller Ergebnisverantwortung — von der Konzeption über Versuch und Prototyp bis zum belastbaren Nachweis. Du bekommst Ziele, keine Arbeitsanweisungen.

Du arbeitest direkt mit unserem CTO und Projektleiter zusammen und sorgst dafür, dass zum jeweiligen Meilenstein die richtigen Prototypen bereitstehen — und koordinierst dafür Kolleginnen, Kollegen und externe Partner.

Aufgaben

Eigenverantwortliche Arbeitspakete:

  • Konzeption und Umsetzung abgegrenzter Entwicklungsthemen

  • Festlegung von Vorgehen, Umfang und Abbruchkriterien

  • Abstimmung mit QM/Regulatory und externen Partnern

  • Terminverantwortung für die Bereitstellung von Versuchsaufbauten, Prototypen und Mustern

Schwerpunkt: Versuch, Prüfaufbau und Labor

  • Aufbau, Inbetriebnahme und Weiterentwicklung von Prüfvorrichtungen, Messplätzen und Versuchsständen

  • Planung, Durchführung und Auswertung von Entwicklungs- und Verifikationsversuchen, unter anderem zu Verdampfungsleistung, Dosiergenauigkeit, Temperaturverhalten, Dichtheit und Lebensdauer

  • Aufbau und Betreuung der Messtechnik inklusive Kalibrierung und Prüfmittelverwaltung

  • Vorbereitung, Begleitung und Auswertung von Prüfkampagnen bei externen Laboren und Hochschulen

  • Erstellung von Versuchsplänen, Versuchsprotokollen, Prüf- und Entwicklungsberichten

Ergänzend: Konstruktion und Prototyping

  • Konstruktion von Vorrichtungen, Adaptern und Bauteilen im CAD

  • Prototyping mittels 3D-Druck sowie Aufbau, Kennzeichnung und Rückverfolgbarkeit von Mustern

  • Technische Bewertung von Bauteilen und Werkstoffen aus Keramik, Spritzguss und Silikon

  • Zuarbeit zur technischen Dokumentation gemäß MDR und ISO 13485

Qualifikation

Damit du in dieser Position erfolgreich bist, solltest du Folgendes mitbringen:

  • Abgeschlossenes technisches Studium (z. B. Maschinenbau, Medizintechnik, Verfahrenstechnik, Physik) oder Technikerabschluss mit einschlägiger Erfahrung

  • Mind. 5 Jahre Berufserfahrung im technischen Entwicklungsumfeld, davon mehrere Jahre in eigenverantwortlicher Rolle

  • Die Fähigkeit, pragmatisch zu entscheiden, wie weit eine Lösung gehen muss — und das zu begründen

  • Sicheres, repräsentatives Auftreten gegenüber Lieferanten, Prüflaboren und Hochschulen

  • Sicherer Umgang mit Messtechnik sowie mit der Auswertung und Darstellung von Versuchsdaten

  • Sorgfältige, nachvollziehbare Dokumentation deiner Arbeit

  • Hohe Eigenmotivation, Selbststrukturierung und Verantwortungsbewusstsein

  • Schnelle Auffassungsgabe, analytisches Denken und die Bereitschaft, dich tief in technische und regulatorische Themen einzuarbeiten

  • Bereitschaft zur Arbeit vor Ort in Ostfildern sowie zu gelegentlichen Einsätzen bei Partnern und Prüflaboren

  • Ausgeprägte Hands-on-Mentalität: du baust auf, misst und packst selbst an

  • Praktische Erfahrung im CAD, etwa mit SolidWorks, Creo oder Fusion 360

  • Deutsch verhandlungssicher, Englisch sicher in Wort und Schrift

Besonders von Vorteil sind:

  • Erfahrung in der Entwicklung medizinischer Geräte unter EU-MDR

  • Kenntnisse der Qualitätsnormen ISO 9001 und ISO 13485

  • Erfahrung mit Aerosolen, Inhalation, Thermodynamik oder Strömungstechnik

  • Kenntnisse in statistischer Versuchsplanung und Auswertung, etwa Python, Minitab oder R

Benefits

Was wir bieten:

  • Ein Produkt, das in den nächsten Jahren durch die Zulassung geht — deine Versuchsergebnisse entscheiden mit darüber, ob es funktioniert

  • Eigene Verantwortungsbereiche mit Entscheidungsspielraum — und die Perspektive, daraus Teilprojektleitung zu machen

  • Arbeiten auf Augenhöhe in einem kleinen, vielseitigen Engineeringteam

  • Schnelle Übernahme von Verantwortung, hoher Gestaltungsspielraum und direkter Einfluss auf den Produkterfolg

  • Kurze Wege: Entwicklung, Labor und Prototypenbau an einem Standort statt verteilter Abstimmungsschleifen

  • Ein Team, das KI-Werkzeuge nicht diskutiert, sondern baut

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten, 30 Tage Urlaub, unbefristete Vollzeitanstellung

  • Mobiles Arbeiten für Auswerte- und Dokumentationstage nach Absprache

Gestalte mit Alveon MedTech die Zukunft der Medizintechnik im Bereich der Inhalation. Wenn du Lust hast, ein Gerät nicht nur zu rechnen, sondern es zu bauen, zu messen und zum Funktionieren zu bringen, freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung — gerne formlos mit Lebenslauf und einem kurzen Wort dazu, warum diese Rolle zu dir passt. Zeugnisse brauchen wir erst später.

Your Mission:

Join VÆRIDION on our journey to develop the world’s first electric nine-seater aircraft.

As Head of Propulsion Battery System (PBS), you will lead VÆRIDION’s PBS department and hold overall technical accountability for the Microliner’s propulsion battery system. The propulsion battery system encompasses the battery cells and packs, the battery management system, high-voltage power distribution and protection, thermal management, charging, and all interfaces to the aircraft, the electric propulsion system and the ground infrastructure.

Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, you will lead a multidisciplinary organisation of around 20 engineers, and growing, spanning electrical systems architecture, airborne electronics, airborne software, cell technology, high-voltage electrical systems, mechanical design and integration, and thermal management. You will set the technical direction, build the organisation and its development processes, and take the propulsion battery system from concept through development, qualification and certification to production readiness.

You will also own the intellectual property strategy for the propulsion battery system, represent VÆRIDION on technical matters towards authorities, industrial partners and funding bodies, and contribute your expertise to other key technologies of the Microliner.

About CodeRabbit

CodeRabbit is the governance and control layer for agentic software development, helping engineering teams trust the code they ship. AI can generate code faster than people can review and understand it. Teams still need to know whether each change solves the right problem, fits their architecture, and is safe to ship.

We provide independent validation grounded in codebase context and team standards, giving people the evidence they need to judge what should ship. Across Review, Triage, Explain, and Secure, our platform challenges changes before merge, prioritizes pull requests by value, impact, and risk, explains what changed and why it matters, and monitors the codebase for security vulnerabilities after merge.

CodeRabbit serves nearly 20,000 customers and supports approximately 300,000 open-source repositories, performing over 2 million code reviews each week. Our $143M Series C, raised at a $1.5B valuation, supports further product development and international expansion.

Almost every company running SAP faces the same task: the move to SAP S/4HANA. These programmes run for years, cost tens of millions, and regularly stall at the same point. Nobody fully understands the legacy landscape that has grown over decades.

That is where Qorelo comes in. We are building the AI platform for S/4HANA transformation. Qorelo reads code, processes, documentation and how the system is actually used, makes the existing landscape transparent, and delivers the fit-to-standard analysis in weeks instead of months. We take a clean core, target-architecture-first approach and carry it end to end across SAP Activate, from Discover to Realize. The knowledge stays with the customer afterwards, long after the system integrators have moved on.

We've raised $3.5M from HPI Ventures, the fund tied to the institute of SAP co-founder Hasso Plattner, along with other strong backers. We already work with Fortune 500 and DAX 40 companies, including Mercedes-Benz.

We are looking for our first Head of Product. You own what Qorelo builds and why, and you build the product function around it. You lead our solution architects, the people who carry our SAP domain depth, you work hand in hand with our Head of Product Design and the engineering team, and you report directly to the C-level.

This is a leadership role at an early-stage company, which means two things at once. You set product strategy and make the big roadmap calls together with the founders, and you still write the spec, sit in the customer workshop and draw the cut line when it matters. Your decisions show up in the product within weeks, running inside some of the largest SAP landscapes in Europe.

• Product strategy. Where Qorelo goes across the transformation lifecycle, which problems we solve first and which we deliberately leave to others. You turn that into a roadmap the whole company understands.
• The roadmap and the calls behind it. You prioritise with evidence from customers, Proofs of Value and the market, and you can defend every call to the founders, to sales and to engineering.
• The product team. You lead our two solution architects today and grow the product team as we scale: hiring, coaching and setting the bar.

• Discovery with real users. Consultants, SAP leads and transformation teams use Qorelo inside live programmes. You and your team sit with them, see where the product wins and where it falls short, and bring that back as decisions, not just notes.
• Product in the sales cycle. You join key customer and partner conversations, shape Proofs of Value with sales, and make sure what we promise matches what we ship.

• The bridge between SAP and AI. SAP depth on one side, an AI-native engineering team on the other. You speak enough of both languages that nothing gets lost, and together with our solution architects you make sure what we ship is usable by SAP people, not just correct.
• Shipping and outcomes. Specs, acceptance criteria, tradeoffs, cut lines and success metrics. Features reach real users on real landscapes, and you own whether they landed.

What you need
• 6+ years of professional experience, with deep hands-on SAP experience: S/4HANA transformation, fit-to-standard, and module-level depth in at least one core area such as FI/CO, SD, MM or PP. Whether you come from SAP consulting, solution architecture or product at an SAP ecosystem software company, all of it counts.
• 4+ years in product: you've owned a B2B product and its roadmap end to end, prioritised with engineering and shipped to enterprise users. Title doesn't matter, ownership does.
• Experience leading people: you have led product managers, solution architects or consultants, and you want to keep building a team.
• A command of the SAP transformation lifecycle and SAP Activate deep enough to be credible with CIOs, Heads of SAP and senior consultants at enterprise clients.
• Strong AI curiosity: you've actually built or worked hands-on with LLM tooling and formed opinions about where it breaks.
• Comfort in an early-stage environment: ambiguity, speed, hands-on work alongside strategy.
• Fluent English. German is a plus for our DACH client base, but not expected.
You might be a fit if
• You've sat inside an S/4HANA programme and thought ""half of this should be software"", and you can name which half.
• Consultants trust you on module questions and engineers trust you to write a clear spec.
You've taken a product from its first enterprise customers to something repeatable, and you know what you would do differently next time.
• You know the SAP tool landscape, from Cloud ALM to Signavio and LeanIX, and where the gaps between them are.
• You want your product decisions to run inside DAX 40 landscapes within weeks, not sit in a committee for quarters.

What we offer
• Real ownership. A seat at the leadership table, meaningful equity and a direct hand in the company's direction. We're looking for people who want to shape a company, not join one.
• Competitive salary, benchmarked for product leadership in Berlin.
• The problems. Fortune 500 and DAX 40 production landscapes, including Mercedes-Benz. Your roadmap runs at the core of companies most product leaders only read about.
• The team. Short paths, fast decisions, and a direct line to the founders, engineers and architects who build what you define.
• 25 days paid vacation plus German public holidays.
• Company offsites with the whole team.
• An office at the Wasserturm in Prenzlauer Berg. This role works from the office, because product decisions here happen in the room with the architects and engineers.
• Wellhub membership, top-tier equipment and access to the latest AI tools.
1. Intro call with our CTO Marino (30 min)
2. Deep dive on your SAP and product background with Louis, our CEO (45 min)
3. On-site workshop: a product strategy exercise with the team, including our solution architects and our Head of Product Design

Finance Assistant

Edinburgh

Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the legal operations platform for in-house teams, and we’re growing fast.


We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems.

Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgment matters, and every step is captured as work happens.

We’re built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend, and become a function the business can run with.

More than 500 companies use Wordsmith. We’ve raised over $80m from leading investors, and we’re building one of the defining companies in legal AI — from our office in Edinburgh.

You won’t be joining a big, process-heavy finance function. You’ll be one of the first Finance hires, working on a brand new, AI-native ERP system (Rillet) with the freedom to actually improve how things are done — not just keep the lights on.

If you want real exposure to the business, a seat close to the founders and leadership team, and the chance to shape processes rather than inherit them, this is that seat.

As Finance Assistant, you’ll own the day-to-day mechanics that keep Wordsmith’s finances running — cash, invoicing, collections, payables and expenses — and you’ll have the tools and the licence to automate as much of it as possible.

  • Complete daily cash reconciliation across our accounts

We’re a fast-moving, Edinburgh-based Legal AI company that’s just raised over $80m. Joining now means joining early enough to shape how our finance function is built — with modern tools, real ownership, and a team that wants to do things properly rather than just keep pace.

Normal Computing | Build with Us

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London.

The Role

Validating conventional silicon is a solved discipline. Validating silicon that computes with noise is not, and you will be the one who figures out how. As our FPGA Design Engineer, you will own the bridge between RTL and physical silicon: bringing our physics-inspired ASIC designs to life on FPGA platforms for pre-silicon validation and early software development, and building the test infrastructure for post-silicon bring-up and characterization. Your scope spans the entire FPGA lifecycle: selecting hardware platforms, implementing complex RTL, debugging in the lab, and writing the software that drives it all, working daily with our silicon, EDA, and research teams.

incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Notion, Linear, Ramp and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

The role in one line

Commercial AE is where incident.io's growth gets made real - you're in front of the most ambitious digital-native companies out there, and the deals you close show up in the trajectory of the whole business.

What that looks like day to day

This is a full-cycle AE role with a strong outbound bias. Yes, inbound comes in - but the AEs who thrive here are the ones who don't wait for it. You'll own your own pipeline from the ground up, building target lists, running creative outreach campaigns, and picking up the phone without being asked twice. Outbound here is a craft, not a numbers game.

You'll be selling into VP Engineering, CTO, and SRE leaders at some of the most forward-thinking digital-native companies in the world. Deals typically land in the $40k–$50k range with a clear path into six figures, and a sales cycle of around 45 days means you're moving fast and closing regularly.

We run a pod model - you'll work closely with a BDR and Solutions Engineer rather than whoever happens to be free. That means real partnerships, shared context, and accountability that goes both ways. You'll also work alongside CS from early in the deal, which means handoffs that don't lose the thread.

What makes the selling here different is the product and the story behind it. incident.io is an AI-native platform built by engineers, for engineers - our founders have been on-call, they've felt the 2am page, and they built something to fix it. When you're in a room with a CTO or an SRE lead, you're not pitching software - you're talking to someone about a problem they've lived, and you understand it. That's the edge.

AEs here are AI-forward in how they operate - whether that's building business cases, running research, or finding smarter ways to work a territory. We expect you to bring ideas, not just execute a playbook.

About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure
column2:
it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

How we work

We're in the middle of a deliberate shift in how hx builds. Everyone in product development is a Builder, and the Product Engineer is the default unit of how we work.

We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods, usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships. Your growth sits elsewhere: a Career Mentor owns your development and progression, so you can move to where the most important problem is without your career following the org chart.

We hire Product Engineers into hx, not into a fixed team, domain, or layer of the stack. You'll start in the stream where your strengths and our highest-value problems meet, and move as the problems move.

Product Engineers are T-shaped: deep expertise in software engineering, plus enough product and design judgement to make routine calls yourself. An embedded PM or designer raises a pod's ceiling on the hardest problems, but is never a gate between you and the customer. This is also a deliberately AI-native role, and one of the areas where we're moving fastest.

A pod of three owns its problem whole, which means going wherever it leads: front end, back end, data, or infrastructure. You don't need to be full-stack by trade, but you do need to be comfortable working outside your strongest layer.

The Product Engineer role is the same at every level. What scales is the size of the problem you own, how expensive your decisions are to reverse, and how far your judgement travels beyond your pod. At Level 2, that looks like this:
column4:
margin-bottom:0px""> 

What you'll be doing

  • Taking a customer problem from discovery to production inside a pod, getting close to customers yourself, framing the problem, and shipping in small increments guided by real customer signal rather than internal opinion.

  • Directing AI agents to draft implementation, tests, and migrations, then reviewing, integrating, and hardening that work. You'll write intent precisely enough to brief both a teammate and an agent, and own correctness and maintainability regardless of how the first draft was produced.

  • Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve.

  • Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting.

  • Moving between pods, problems, and streams as priorities change, ramping fast on unfamiliar domains and leaving what you built running well behind you.

  • Taking full accountability for outcomes rather than just your code changes: raising risks early, and deciding rather than escalating.

What you'll need to have done

  • Built and shipped production systems end-to-end, from design through rollout, monitoring, and iteration, in settings where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency mattered.

  • Designed testing and observability that made complex behaviour understandable, debuggable, and safe to evolve.

  • Worked effectively in a polyglot environment, choosing the right tool for the problem and picking up unfamiliar languages, domains, and codebases fast. Strong systems experience, for example in Rust, C/C++, or Python, is valued, and we'll upskill you where there are gaps.

  • Shipped work outside your strongest layer of the stack when the problem needed it, picking up the front end, the data layer, or the infrastructure rather than waiting for someone else to.

  • Used AI tools as a serious part of how you build, with the judgement to direct, review, and stand behind what they produce.

  • Carried product and design judgement into your engineering work, shaping the solution rather than only implementing a spec and making sensible calls under ambiguity.

  • Owned outcomes beyond your immediate task, taking decisions rather than escalating them.

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn’t obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you’ll do your best work. We’re building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Because we’re building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don’t always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that’s competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Company

NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.

Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.

Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.

Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.

Role

We are looking for a skilled Thermal Engineer with experience in spacecraft thermal management at both the subsystem and spacecraft level.

You’ll work closely with a cross-functional team - including mechanical, propulsion, electronics, and mission planning - to ensure reliable thermal performance of our satellite throughout all mission phases: from launch to operation in orbit and end-of-life.

You should be capable of delivering a thermal control system from scratch and taking full ownership of it, ensuring the success of our mission.

  • Perform steady-state and transient thermal analysis of the spacecraft across all mission phases (TVAC testing, launch, orbit).

  • Design and implement thermal control solutions such as multilayer insulation (MLI), radiators, heaters, thermo-optical coatings, thermistors, and thermal straps

  • Develop and support thermal vacuum (TVAC) test procedures, instrumentation setup, and post-test data analysis.

  • Be hands on in hardware testing for validation of processes, instrumentation, and materials and components chosen for in house developments

  • Solid understanding of thermal engineering principles in the context of spacecraft systems.

  • Hands-on experience with thermal simulation tools such as Systema, Thermal Desktop, ESATAN, or equivalent.

    validation).

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, iterative development environment.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience designing or testing spacecraft thermal systems.

  • Exposure to multidisciplinary space system development or mission analysis.

  • Equity and competitive salary - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.

  • Comprehensive benefits - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups.

Founded in 1994, Prosci is a global leader in change management and the provider of choice for 80% of Fortune 100 companies. Prosci combines scientific research with the people side of change to deliver results-focused solutions that enable clients to achieve change outcomes and grow organizational change capability. Health can’t wait.

Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.

Alan exists to end the wait.

Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.

So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.

We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture. We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.

Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.

⭐ SECURITY ASSOCIATE INTERNSHIP ⭐

Six-month end-of-studies internship in Paris.

Looking for an end-of-studies internship where you do real cybersecurity work, not a side project nobody uses? Alan protects the health data of more than 1M members, and keeping it safe is part of everyday work here.

You join the Security team as a full member for six months. Meet Arago and the Aragonians

Arago is an AI and computer hardware company whose mission is to drive the course of history forward. We do so by accelerating breakthroughs at the intersection of AI and semiconductors.

Founded in 2024 by AI researchers and physicists with deep expertise in photonics, electronics, software, mathematics, and machine learning, Arago brings together a lean team of engineers and scientists from the world’s top companies and research labs.

Composed of nine nationalities and operating from hubs in France, North America, and Israel, we believe in great science and fast achievements. Our work is guided by these core principles:

  1. Do great things: we deliver work we’re proud to sign our name to.

  2. High velocity: speed matters. We move quickly, one step at a time.

  3. One unit: we’re all in this together, with relationships grounded in trust, respect, and camaraderie.

Arago is backed by executives from Apple, Arm, Nvidia, Microsoft, and Hugging Face, as well as prominent US and European deeptech venture firms and exited founders.

As a Senior Packaging Engineer, you will lead IC packaging initiatives from conceptualization and design to manufacturing process selection. You will establish the necessary supply chain, manage sub-contractors, and oversee the NPI and ramp-up phases for current and future Arago devices.

  • Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or Integrated Circuits Design.
