For decades, the consumer side of those conversations sucked: long queues, robotic menus, repeated explanations, and advice that is often unhelpful. Most people today still cannot simply say what their problem is in natural language when communicating with businesses.

AI changes that. For the first time, companies can have natural conversations with customers at massive scale. Every B2C company - from energy providers to telcos to insurers - will use AI agents to talk to their customers. The number of conversations businesses will handle is going to explode in the coming years.

At telli, we are solving the challenges that come with that shift. Today, leading B2C companies like Sky are already using telli to deploy thousands of voice agents to provide their customers with a new experience. But building a first voice agent is easy, getting it to drive real outcomes for customers and businesses is the hard part. telli helps companies build, deploy, and improve consumer-facing AI voice agents at scale. This will become one of the most important software categories of the next decade, and we intend to win it.

We are a small, AI-pilled team that likes to solve hard problems. Be it engineering, product, or GTM - we build, experiment, and move fast, while heavily leveraging the capabilities of AI models. All of us like to challenge ourselves and take real ownership over what we do, all while still staying humble and keeping a low-ego culture.

Check out our principles to see how we work.

Your mission

telli is arriving in France. We are building a small, mighty team in Paris to make every customer interaction worth having. We have a product already used by leading B2C businesses, but the French market is still at the beginning. We will earn our place, one customer at a time.

We are outbound first. As a founding Enterprise Account Executive, you will create opportunities, win major French accounts, and help define how telli sells in this market. You will carry a quota and own the hard parts of the deal, from the first cold conversation to signature. Your work will shape the playbook for the team that follows.

What you'll do

  • Build your own enterprise pipeline through thoughtful outbound, calls, referrals, and a deep understanding of French customer operations.

  • Lead complex sales cycles end to end: discovery, demos, business cases, executive alignment, security, legal, procurement, and negotiation.

  • Find the real problem behind a customer's interest in AI, quantify the value of solving it, and earn trust across the buying group.

  • Work closely with the France team, founders, product, and deployment colleagues to turn early customers into lasting successes.

  • Keep an honest forecast and turn wins, losses, and objections into a repeatable French sales motion.

What makes you a great fit

  • You have personally sourced and closed complex B2B enterprise deals, ideally in software or AI, and can show how you earned them.

  • You are comfortable speaking with senior business leaders and working through IT, security, finance, legal, and procurement.

  • You enjoy the unglamorous work as much as the big meeting: prospecting, follow-up, and fixing what is broken.

  • You bring a bias for action, aim for excellence, take ownership, and work with low ego. Read the telli principles

  • You communicate with confidence and care in French and can work effectively in English with our international team.

  • You are based in Paris and can spend two weeks in Berlin for onboarding. You are ready to travel and visit prospects across France when needed.

You may not be a good fit if

  • You don't believe voice is the future of how people and businesses talk to each other.

  • You expect a ready-made book of business or marketing to build your pipeline.

  • You want to join deals only after discovery, and avoid cold outreach or the hard follow-through between meetings.

  • You need a fixed playbook before acting or pass on ownership when a deal gets messy.

  • You dislike working across executive, operations, IT, legal, and procurement stakeholders or learning openly from losses.

The reality of the role

France is a new market for us. There is no mature local playbook or book of business waiting for you. Some deals will be messy, and you will need to create momentum yourself. If you want ownership, direct feedback, ambitious colleagues, and the chance to do the best work of your career, this is the opportunity.

The hiring process

The hiring process itself is a case study in how you sell. Approach it as you would a complex account: research us, form a point of view, earn attention, ask and listen, follow through, and respond to feedback. We will evaluate how you create momentum and manage the process end to end, with the judgment and ownership you would bring to winning enterprise customers in France.

Compensation

€120,000–€180,000 gross annual on-target earnings (OTE), with a 50% base salary and 50% variable compensation at target, plus equity. We will discuss the equity terms during the hiring process.

About Hexa

Hexa (formerly eFounders) gives entrepreneurs the best chances to build outstanding companies.

We are a pioneering, world-leading startup studio born in Europe that designs, builds and launches category-defining startups. We are today recognized as one of the best venture studios in the world, with a track record comparable to tier-1 VC funds.

We have created 60+ companies (including 3 unicorns) with a combined valuation of over $5 billion, among them Aircall, Spendesk, Front, Swan and Yousign.

Hexa is in full growth mode, with three early-stage activities: our Ventures programs Hexa Start and Hexa Sprint which help entrepreneurs go from zero to one, and a PE program, Hexa Scale, which takes majority stakes in existing startups and pushes them to new thresholds.

The hardware vertical at Hexa: Frontier Tech

Frontier Tech is Hexa’s studio focused on physical tech, led by Guerric de Crombrugghe.

We build companies that move atoms: real machines, deployed in the field, often for defense, energy, space and critical infrastructure. A few examples of what is on the bench today include containerized atmospheric water generators, expendable turbojets, and ship-borne satellite ground stations.

Our edge is velocity. We go from idea to working hardware with small teams and lean budgets, against legacy players with hundreds of engineers and decade-long programs. AI is now the biggest lever we have to widen that gap, today by speeding up how we build, and tomorrow by shaping what kind of companies we build.

Why this role, why now

AI for hardware is moving faster than any team can track. Our internal map now tracks close to 200 tools, from text-to-CAD, AI-native electronics and physics surrogates to manufacturing, test data, procurement and the MCP connectors that let agents drive CAD and EDA tools directly.

Most of these tools will not matter. A handful will cut weeks off our programs. We need someone whose job is to find those, prove them on our real parts, and put them in the hands of our founders before our competitors do.

The mission

We’re looking for an industrial hardware engineer who is 100% AI-pilled, with a dual objective:

  • Adopt AI inside our startups. Make every Frontier Tech venture the fastest-moving hardware team in its category, using the best AI tools available today.

  • Build companies that grow with AI. Design products and business models that are both AI-enabled (they get better with every new generation of models) and AI-enablers (they feed AI with the data, compute, energy or infrastructure it needs), and run the companies themselves on AI from day one. The goal is a positive feedback loop: the more AI grows, the more our companies grow.

Adoption is the immediate focus. The role splits into two:

80%: deploy AI inside our ventures

Hands-on, embedded in the teams, measured by weeks saved.

  • Map the bottlenecks. Sit with each venture and map its engineering workflow, from requirements to design, simulation, electronics, firmware, test, manufacturing and documentation. Find the steps that cost the most weeks.

  • Do the engineering. You are part of the team, not an advisor. You will run the CAD, set up the simulations, push the PCB, write the firmware agent, build the digital twin, produce the documentation, build the tools that automate technical pre-sales material that wins a contract. You ship parts and files, not slides.

  • Run the shared AI infrastructure. Set up and maintain the agents, repos and connectors between tools (CAD, EDA, simulation, data), with a common setup across ventures, so founders spend their time engineering rather than configuring.

  • Make it stick. Start with hands-on workshops on each team’s real problems, then train founders and engineers, write the playbooks, and track real adoption so tools are used every day rather than demoed once.

20%: studio radar and partnerships

  • Keep the map alive. Track the AI-for-hardware landscape and what frontier labs ship, and maintain our living map of tools, maturity and pricing.

  • See beyond the hype. Our founders want evidence, not promises. Benchmark tools on our own parts and problems, not on vendor demos, and tell the studio plainly where the value is and where it is not.

  • Close partnerships. Negotiate studio-wide deals with key players (early access, design-partner status, credits, preferential pricing) so every Hexa hardware venture starts with better conditions than it could get alone.

  • Build the default stack. Turn what works into a reusable AI toolkit that every new Frontier Tech venture gets on day one.

  • Design AI-native companies. Work with founders from day one on where AI sits in the product, how the business model captures value as models improve, which data to capture and own, and which workflows run on agents so the team scales without headcount growing in step with revenue.

Who we’re looking for

  • An industrial hardware engineer. 3 to 7 years designing, building and testing physical products in aerospace, defense, energy, automotive, industrial equipment or a hardware startup. You have taken parts from CAD to the shop floor and know tolerancing, DFM, test campaigns and suppliers.

  • 100% AI-pilled. You use AI agents every day, you have built your own automations, and you have already tried text-to-CAD, AI simulation or AI electronics tools on real work. You switch setups as soon as something better ships, and you have opinions on how a hardware company should be built when much of its engineering is done by agents.

  • A skeptical builder. You judge tools by measured time saved, not by launch videos. You are as happy killing a tool as adopting one.

  • High agency and fast. You figure it out and ship without waiting to be told how. You are comfortable jumping between projects in the same week.

  • Commercial sense and pedagogy. Comfortable in front of founders, engineers and vendors, able to run a workshop that turns skeptics into users, and to negotiate a partnership that actually benefits our ventures.

  • Languages and location. Working in English, based in Paris or Brussels, with regular days physically with the founding teams.

Recruitment process

  • First call with Laure, Talent Partner at Hexa

  • Interview with Guerric: mutual introduction, deep dive into the role and how we work.

  • Case study: a real engineering problem from one of our ventures with Tanguy, Hexa's CTO. Propose an AI-augmented workflow and run it as a short hands-on workshop with the founders, with at least one tool working live

  • Cultural fit interview with Matthieu (CEO)

About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

As an AI Deployment Strategist with Science Focus, you will drive the adoption and deployment of Mistral's AI solutions for science-heavy projects, working closely with customers from strategic vision to production implementation in domains like computer vision, robotics, and embodied AI.

This role sits at the intersection of deep technical expertise, business strategy, and hands-on deployment, ensuring our customers achieve transformative outcomes in specialized AI applications.

You will partner with senior executives to design AI roadmaps for science-driven use cases, collaborate with the Applied AI and Research teams to deliver solutions in production, and ensure seamless transitions from presales to postsales. Your work will directly contribute to expanding Mistral's capabilities in cutting-edge AI domains.

column17:
>Le projet ERC vise à évaluer la capacité de stockage de composites innovants en biocarbones. Il s’agit d’une famille de matériaux carbonés avancés et durables issus de la biomasse, permettant de stocker l’énergie dans différents environnements, contrairement à la plupart des solutions actuelles reposant sur des matériaux d’origine fossile ou non durables. Cela devrait se traduire par une réduction notable des émissions de CO₂ et des économies d’énergie. Les travaux seront menés dans un environnement international, avec des visites régulières dans les laboratoires de partenaires en France, en Inde et aux États-Unis.

Nous recherchons un chercheur ou une chercheuse très motivé(e) pour contribuer à la conception et au développement de matériaux et de dispositifs de stockage de l’énergie avancés et performants, en combinant des méthodes de calcul, l’intelligence artificielle (IA) et des approches expérimentales.
column18: >L’objectif est de développer et d’appliquer des modèles numériques, des méthodes fondées sur les données et des outils utilisant l’IA afin de prédire les propriétés des matériaux, d’optimiser leur composition et leur structure, et d’améliorer la capacité et les performances de stockage de l’énergie. Les travaux combineront des études théoriques et numériques avec la synthèse expérimentale, la caractérisation, la validation et l’optimisation de solutions innovantes de stockage de l’énergie.
column19: >Un axe important du projet portera sur l’étude des propriétés thermophysiques, thermomécaniques et de stabilité thermique de composites à base de biocarbone graphitique. Le/La candidat(e) étudiera les relations entre la structure des matériaux, leurs propriétés fonctionnelles, leur comportement et les performances globales du dispositif en conditions d’utilisation, afin de contribuer au développement de technologies de stockage de l’énergie sûres, efficaces et durables.

column2:
Social Controlling Analyst assure le pilotage de la masse salariale et des effectifs, tout en développant une approche analytique et data-driven de la fonction RH.

Il/elle garantit la fiabilité des données sociales, contribue à la construction et au suivi du budget RH, automatise les reportings et transforme les données RH en analyses pertinentes en étroite collaboration avec la Direction Financière.
column3:
>

Principales responsabilités

A. Contrôle de gestion sociale et pilotage de la masse salariale

  • Construire le budget annuel de masse salariale et des effectifs, en lien avec la DRH, la Direction Financière et les équipes opérationnelles.

  • Élaborer les prévisions actualisées (forecasts) et les projections de fin d'année.

  • Analyser les écarts entre réalisé, budget et prévisions, et identifier les principaux facteurs explicatifs.

  • Modéliser les effets des évolutions d'effectifs, des augmentations salariales, des promotions, des bonus, des départs et des recrutements.

  • Réaliser des simulations financières pour accompagner les décisions RH : recrutements, réorganisations, politiques de rémunération et évolution des effectifs.

  • Suivre les principaux indicateurs économiques et sociaux : masse salariale, effectifs, rémunération moyenne, coûts des recrutements et autres coûts RH.

  • Contribuer à l'amélioration des processus de contrôle et de fiabilisation des données de paie et de rémunération.

  • Préparer les analyses nécessaires aux revues budgétaires et aux présentations destinées au CODIR.

B. HR Data Analytics et aide à la décision

  • Exploiter et croiser les données issues du SIRH, de la paie, du recrutement et des autres outils RH.

  • Analyser les tendances RH et identifier les principaux facteurs d'évolution des indicateurs sociaux.

  • Réaliser des analyses approfondies sur le turnover, l'absentéisme, le recrutement, la mobilité interne, les rémunérations et les parcours professionnels.

  • Identifier les populations, métiers ou entités nécessitant une attention particulière et formuler des recommandations opérationnelles.

  • Développer des analyses permettant d'évaluer l'efficacité des politiques RH et d'en mesurer les résultats.

  • Concevoir des analyses prospectives et, lorsque les données le permettent, des modèles de prévision pour anticiper les évolutions des effectifs et des indicateurs sociaux.

  • Traduire les résultats des analyses en recommandations compréhensibles et directement exploitables par les équipes RH et les managers.

  • Concevoir, maintenir et faire évoluer les tableaux de bord RH et les reportings destinés à la DRH, au CODIR et aux équipes opérationnelles.

  • Automatiser la production des reportings récurrents afin de réduire les tâches manuelles et de sécuriser les résultats.

  • Développer des dashboards interactifs permettant de suivre les indicateurs clés et d'analyser les données par métier, entité, pays, population ou niveau hiérarchique.

  • Harmoniser les définitions, les règles de calcul et les référentiels des indicateurs RH.

  • Contribuer à l'amélioration de la qualité, de la cohérence et de la disponibilité des données sociales.

  • Participer à l'évolution des outils de reporting et à l'optimisation des processus de collecte et d'exploitation des données.

We're a group of friends building apps for friends, and we think friendship deserves a better place online. Our brand is how the world first meets that idea, usually in a three-second scroll, in a language that isn't ours, on a phone in a city we've never been to.


We're looking for a Brand Lead who writes like a dream and ships like a machine. Someone who's run global campaigns at a top agency, knows what a great brief feels like, and is ready to trade the client side of the table for owning the whole thing.


You'll shape how amo sounds, looks and shows up everywhere, from a two-word push notification to a launch film watched in fifteen countries.

What you'll do:

  • Own the amo voice. Write it, guard it, and make it better every week. App copy, launch posts, store listings, social, scripts, the little lines that make people smile.

  • Run global campaigns end to end. From the first idea on a napkin to the last cut in market, across Europe, the US and beyond.

  • Brief and push creative partners. Agencies, directors, creators and our in-house design team. You know how to get their best work because you've been on their side of the table.

  • Make the brand local without making it boring. Adapt ideas so they land in Paris, London, LA and Seoul, not just translate them.

  • Measure what the brand is really doing. Set up and run brand tracking across our markets, following awareness, consideration and perception over time, and turn what you learn into the next brief.

  • Work in days, not weeks. Spot a moment on Tuesday, have a campaign live on Thursday, learn from it on Friday.

  • Sweat the details. Easter eggs, onboarding screens, the name of a feature. Small words do big work here.

What that may look like:

Kicking off a campaign with an agency for our next market launch, and setting up the tracker that tells us a month later whether people there know who we are and like what they see.

Who you are:

  • A writer first. You can make a headline sing and kill your darlings without blinking. Your portfolio proves it.

  • Agency-trained. You've spent real time at a creative agency and worked on brands people actually know. You've sat in the pitch, survived the feedback round and shipped anyway.

  • Global from day one. You've led or played a key role in campaigns that ran across several markets at once, and you know what changes (and what never should) from one country to the next.

  • Fast and opinionated. Conviction over consensus. You'd rather put out something great today than something perfect next month.

  • Fluent in internet. You know what's trending before it trends, and you can tell the difference between a moment worth joining and one worth skipping.

  • Bilingual or better is a plus. English is our working language. French, Spanish, Portuguese, Korean or Japanese would make us very happy.

Bonus points if:

You've worked on a consumer app, built a brand from scratch, or have a group chat that's funnier than most ad campaigns.

Why amo:

  • You'll own it. No account director, no client sign-off chain. Your ideas go from your head to millions of phones.

  • You'll move fast. We make decisions quickly and learn from mistakes even quicker. Intense, but healthy.

  • You'll be in good company. Over half the team is international, with 25 nationalities and counting. One in four of us moved cities or countries to be here.

  • You'll grow x10. Colleagues across product, design, engineering and growth will challenge your work every day, and you'll do the same to theirs.

  • You'll have backing. We're supported by some of the best tier-1 investors in the world and growing at a pace our space hasn't seen in years.

Life at amo:

To ensure that everyone is set up for success within our way of working, we work together onsite 5 days a week. We wanted to make sure coming to the office is as comfortable as possible for you:

Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

Please apply with a CV in the English Language. This is a Paris-based role with global reach and therefore Fluency in French and English (both written and spoken) is important.

Role Summary

Checkout.com is seeking a talented and dynamic Legal Counsel with a strong French employment law background to join our Employment Legal team. This role will involve advising on the full spectrum of employment law issues across our French business and supporting broader global employment law initiatives, especially across other EMEA jurisdictions.

You will work closely with our People Team and key business stakeholders in France and internationally. This is a great opportunity to support and develop our French employment legal strategy while collaborating as part of a global team supporting employees across EMEA, APAC, and the Americas. You will take a consultative and commercial approach to handling complex Labor Code compliance matters, works council (CSE) consultations, litigation, employee relations, and strategic projects across France. You’ll also advise on individual and collective dismissals, restructurings, settlement negotiations, performance management, misconduct investigations and HR audits. You’ll monitor legal and regulatory developments across EMEA and provide proactive guidance on emerging risks and legal requirements. You’ll also help the employment legal team develop scalable processes, templates, and compliance frameworks, including through the use of AI tools.

You will be able to handle multiple areas of responsibilities autonomously, demonstrating excellent critical judgment with hands-on approach. You will report into our Associate General Counsel (Head of Employment) based in London. You will also work closely with the regional People Team leads, based in France and other EMEA jurisdictions.

You will be joining a high-achieving legal team in one of Europe's most valuable fintechs. Our mission is to be the best legal team in the world, providing pragmatic and commercially focused advice, finding creative solutions to manage risk and becoming trusted advisers to our colleagues in the business.

Essential Qualifications:

  • French qualified lawyer (Avocat admitted to the French Bar or Master 2 in French Employment Law / Droit du Travail)

  • 5+ years experience specializing in French employment law, either in a reputable law firm or in-house

  • Fluency in French and English (both written and spoken) with the ability to articulate complex legal issues clearly to non-French leadership.

  • Within a commutable distance from our Paris office and comfortable working in the office as necessary under our hybrid working policy (currently three days per week on scheduled office days).

Strong candidates will demonstrate the following:

  • Experience as in-house employment counsel, ideally in a large global business headquartered outside of France.

  • Extensive experience managing CSE consultations, collective negotiations, restructurings, and pre-litigation/settlement strategy in France.

  • Work with a high-growth technology or another fast-paced company.

  • Exceptional analytical and writing skills, with a business-centric focus on risk.

  • Excellent time management skills and experience managing a diverse workload and competing stakeholder demands.

  • Enthusiasm for new challenges and working with a range of different stakeholders.

  • Be a systemic thinker with proven abilities for process improvement and simplification, including AI.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity, constant change, and a fast-paced culture.

Role Type and Location

This is a permanent and full-time role based in Paris. Under our current hybrid working policy, office attendance is mandatory on 3 days per week.

Additional Information

If you don't meet all the requirements but think you might still be right for the role, please apply anyway. We're always keen to speak to people who connect with our mission and values.

We believe in equal opportunities

We work as one team. Wherever you come from. However you identify. And whichever payment method you use.

Our clients come from all over the world — and so do we. Hiring hard-working people and giving them a community to thrive in is critical to our success.

When you join our team, we’ll empower you to unlock your potential so you can do your best work. We’d love to hear how you think you could make a difference here with us.

We want to set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable. We’ll be happy to support you.

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

the bottleneck is embedding AI deeply into the core processes of a company to drive an inflection in pace and create organisational advantage. Europe is falling behind on AI, and we exist to help its businesses build real, defensible advantage from it rather than simply adopting it.

As an Applied AI Engineer in Berlin, you’ll build the production AI systems behind Resonance’s client engagements across DACH, driving a dramatic acceleration in productivity or a step change in growth for our key clients. You will work at the AI frontier alongside Senior AI Engineers, owning features, integrations and evals end to end. You’ll build evals and observability from day one, take features from first prototype to production, and deploy and extend what we build inside client environments, shipping at pace with the latest AI coding tools. You’ll grow with the firm by contributing to Resonance’s own AI products and shared platform, turning what you learn on each build into reusable components, and taking on more ownership as you grow.

TLDR: We’re looking for top 1%, high agency, AI-forward graduates to join the first graduate cohort at Resonance in Berlin as Applied AI Engineers. You’ll work at the frontier and solve real problems in an environment that champions ownership, autonomy and innovation at pace.

Who we are

Resonance is an applied AI company. We have recently raised one of the largest ever European seed rounds, with investment from Anthropic and Hg Capital. Our mission is to close the AI diffusion gap and rebuild businesses for the AI era. We're looking to hire Europe’s elite AI talent, and we're building our Berlin hub to serve clients across Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

Why now

We believe the economic diffusion of AI is the major challenge of the next decade. Foundation models are advancing far faster than organisations can absorb them
column2:
the bottleneck is embedding AI deeply into the core processes of a company to drive an inflection in pace and create organisational advantage. Europe is falling behind on AI, and we exist to help its businesses build real, defensible advantage from it rather than simply adopting it.

The role

As a Graduate Applied AI Engineer in Berlin, you’ll build production AI systems for our clients across DACH from your first month, working alongside Senior Applied AI Engineers who review your code and coach you. You’ll ship agents, integrations, data pipelines and evals, working across the stack from the AI layer to the client’s core systems and the interfaces people use. You’ll sit with the people who do the work today, see how AI changes it, and help client teams run and extend what we build. You’ll also contribute to Resonance’s own AI products and shared platform, take on more ownership as you grow, and help shape how we train, build and grow as one of our first graduate cohort.

Your first year: Comprehensive training when you join, covering AI engineering, our platform and how we work with clients. You’ll be on a client team from your first month, in a small team where you know everyone by name, founders included, and work closely with colleagues in London. Nobody expects you to know it all when you start: asking for help early is part of the job, and senior people make time for it. You’ll start as a Junior Engineer and typically become an Engineer within 18–24 months.

What we’re looking for: You take the initiative, learn fast and go looking for hard problems. You’re AI-obsessed, trying new models and tools the day they come out. You’re finishing a degree in Computer Science or a closely related subject, such as Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Data Science or Mathematics with a strong programming component, or you graduated in one in the last two years, and you can show what you’re capable of through your grades, competitions, internships, societies or things you’ve built. You write good code in Python or TypeScript and have built something with LLMs: a project, a hackathon entry or an open-source contribution. A software engineering internship, ideally at a startup or fast-moving product team, AI side projects or a company you founded are a plus, and so is German for client work in DACH. If you don’t tick every box, apply anyway.

What we offer: Competitive total compensation plus equity. Instead of one product at one company, you’ll ship several production AI systems a year across industries, and help build our own AI products and platform. You’ll learn alongside engineers and operators who have embedded AI into 50+ businesses, in a team aiming to be one of the most talent-dense in Europe and worldwide. Europe is falling behind on AI, and every build moves another European business to the right side of the productivity chasm.

Logistics: Berlin, 3+ days a week in the office or at client sites, mostly in DACH and Europe. English is our working language

About Virtual Identity
column3:
margin-bottom:0px""> 

Virtual Identity (VI) is a digital agency built on Human-Centered Business Growth: combining empathy for people with insight from data to drive real digital success. With around 140 colleagues across Freiburg, Munich, Vienna, and Porto (and remote), we cover the full spectrum from Consulting and UX Research to UX/UI Design, Software Development, and Digital Marketing — always learning in close collaboration with our clients.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer at VI, you sit at the intersection of client, product, and engineering. You're not building in isolation from a backlog handed down by someone else — you go into deep, sustained virtual immersion with the client, understand their real operational problems, and ship working software that solves them, fast. You prototype, integrate, and iterate directly with the people who will use what you build, then help harden it into something production-ready with our delivery teams.

You also bring a well-founded understanding of agentic engineering — not just using AI coding assistants, but genuinely understanding how agents plan, use tools, and fail, and applying that thinking to how you build, integrate, and automate in the field.

This role suits someone who's equally comfortable in a client workshop, a codebase, and a data pipeline — and who gets energy from ambiguity rather than needing it resolved before starting.
column5:
margin-bottom:0px""> 

What you will do:

  • Embed with client teams to observe workflows, diagnose bottlenecks, and identify where custom software can create outsized impact.

  • Rapidly prototype and deploy solutions — internal tools, integrations, automations, data pipelines — directly in the client's environment.

  • Translate messy, real-world requirements into working code without waiting for a fully specified brief.

  • Own the full loop: build, deploy, get feedback from actual users within days, iterate.

  • Use agentic engineering practices — not just AI-assisted coding, but designing workflows, automations, and integrations that leverage agents as a core part of the solution, where it genuinely helps the client.

  • Work closely with VI's UX, consulting, and cloud-native engineering teams to transition prototypes into scalable, supportable production systems.

  • Navigate client infrastructure, security constraints, and existing systems (cloud platforms, APIs, legacy tools) pragmatically.

  • Act as a trusted technical voice in client conversations — you can whiteboard an architecture and defend it in the same meeting.

  • Travel to client sites as needed (frequency depends on engagement).

    What we expect:

  • Strong full-stack or cloud-native engineering experience, with a track record of shipping real software, not just prototypes that die in a demo.

  • Comfort working directly with non-technical stakeholders and translating their problems into technical solutions on the fly.

  • Solid grounding in at least one modern backend stack and one frontend stack, plus working knowledge of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).

Fullstack Developer (m/w/d)

Deine Mission

Du entwickelst Anwendungen, die Menschen im Arbeitsalltag tatsächlich Arbeit abnehmen. Von der verständlichen Oberfläche über die Backend-Logik bis zur Anbindung bestehender Systeme.

Bei Agentur Philipp bauen wir KI-Lösungen und individuelle Software für den Mittelstand. Dafür suchen wir einen Fullstack Developer, der Anforderungen hinterfragt, technisch mitdenkt und Anwendungen zuverlässig in den produktiven Einsatz bringt.

Du arbeitest je nach Projekt mit unterschiedlichen Technologien: JavaScript und TypeScript im Frontend, PHP und Laravel, Node.js oder Python im Backend. Gemeinsam mit dem Team wählst du die passende Lösung.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du entwickelst Webanwendungen vom Frontend bis zum Backend und begleitest sie bis zum produktiven Betrieb.

  • Du baust verständliche Benutzeroberflächen mit React, Next.js, Vue.js oder vergleichbaren Frameworks.

  • Du entwickelst Backends und APIs mit PHP und Laravel, Node.js oder Python und FastAPI, passend zu den Anforderungen des Projekts.

  • Du bindest bestehende Kunden-, ERP- und Drittsysteme an und sorgst für einen zuverlässigen Datenaustausch.

  • Du entwirfst Datenmodelle und setzt Geschäftslogik, Benutzerverwaltung, Rollen und Berechtigungen sauber um.

  • Du integrierst KI-Funktionen und automatisierte Workflows in unsere Anwendungen. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit unseren KI- und Automatisierungsentwicklern zusammen.

  • Du sorgst mit Tests, Logging und Fehlerbehandlung dafür, dass Anwendungen auch außerhalb des Idealfalls funktionieren.

  • Du entwickelst bestehende Systeme weiter und behältst Wartbarkeit, Sicherheit und Performance im Blick.

  • Du stimmst technische Anforderungen mit der Projektleitung ab und machst frühzeitig sichtbar, wenn etwas unklar ist oder aufwendiger wird.

  • Du dokumentierst wichtige technische Entscheidungen so, dass andere im Team deine Arbeit nachvollziehen und weiterführen können.

Das bringst du mit

  • Praktische Erfahrung darin, Webanwendungen eigenständig vom Frontend bis zum Backend zu entwickeln und produktiv einzusetzen.

  • Sehr gute Kenntnisse in JavaScript und TypeScript sowie Erfahrung mit React, Next.js, Vue.js oder einem vergleichbaren Frontend-Framework.

  • Gute Kenntnisse in PHP und praktische Erfahrung mit Laravel.

  • Erfahrung mit Node.js oder Python, idealerweise mit einem Backend-Framework wie Express, NestJS oder FastAPI.

  • Sicherer Umgang mit relationalen Datenbanken wie MySQL oder PostgreSQL sowie Erfahrung mit Datenmodellierung und Datenbankmigrationen.

  • Erfahrung mit REST-APIs, Authentifizierung und der Integration externer Systeme.

  • Routine im Umgang mit Git, Docker und gängigen Deployment-Prozessen.

  • Gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sind Voraussetzung. Du kannst Anforderungen, technische Rückfragen und Abstimmungen im Team und mit unseren Kunden sicher auf Deutsch klären.

  • Du denkst an Berechtigungen, Datenschutz und Fehlerfälle, bevor die Anwendung beim Kunden läuft.

  • Du arbeitest dich in bestehende Codebasen und neue Technologien ein. Du musst nicht jedes genannte Framework beherrschen, solltest aber Frontend und Backend sicher abdecken.

  • Du arbeitest eigenständig, sprichst Probleme offen an und bringst übernommene Aufgaben zuverlässig zum Abschluss.

Das ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss

  • Erfahrung mit LLM-APIs, RAG-Systemen oder anderen KI-Funktionen.

  • Erfahrung mit n8n oder vergleichbaren Automatisierungsplattformen.

  • Vertiefte Kenntnisse im Laravel-Ökosystem, beispielsweise Livewire oder Inertia.js.

  • Erfahrung mit ERP-Schnittstellen, Webhooks, Queues, Hintergrundjobs und asynchroner Verarbeitung.

  • Kenntnisse in CI/CD, Linux, Monitoring oder Cloud-Infrastruktur.

  • Erfahrung mit automatisierten Frontend-, Backend- und Integrationstests.

Was dich bei uns erwartet

  • Anwendungen, die bei Kunden im Alltag eingesetzt werden. Du siehst, wofür du entwickelst und was deine Arbeit verändert.

  • Unterschiedliche Aufgaben rund um individuelle Software, KI-Kollegen, Schnittstellen und Prozessautomatisierung.

  • Ein breiter Tech-Stack und technische Entscheidungen, die sich am Projekt orientieren.

  • Technischer Gestaltungsspielraum und die Möglichkeit, unsere Entwicklungsstandards mit aufzubauen.

  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit KI-Entwicklern, Automatisierungsexperten und Projektleitung.

  • Direkter Austausch mit den Menschen, die Entscheidungen treffen. Kurze Wege und schnelle Umsetzung.

  • Remote-freundliches Arbeiten mit regelmäßigem persönlichem Austausch in Dingolfing. Für die finale Gesprächsrunde möchten wir dich vor Ort kennenlernen.

Über Agentur Philipp

Agentur Philipp ist eine KI-Umsetzungsberatung für den Mittelstand. Wir beraten nicht nur, sondern bauen Systeme, die im Alltag funktionieren, Aufwand reduzieren und einen messbaren Unterschied machen.

Unsere Haltung ist klar: Verstehen, Anpacken, Liefern und Besser werden.

Klingt nach dir?

Dann schick uns deinen Lebenslauf, GitHub-, Portfolio- oder Projektlinks und gern eine kurze Beschreibung einer Anwendung, die du selbst produktiv gebaut hast. Was war deine Verantwortung? Welche technische Entscheidung war besonders wichtig? Und wie hast du sichergestellt, dass die Anwendung im Alltag zuverlässig läuft?

Uns interessiert, was du gebaut hast und wie du an Probleme herangehst.

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung.

Neuphonic is building the next generation of voice AI, making natural, real-time speech accessible across devices, languages, and applications.

As our customer base grows, we need to scale our production infrastructure while maintaining the performance, reliability, and low latency that our products depend on.

We're looking for an Infrastructure / Platform Engineer to take ownership of our cloud infrastructure and inference systems. You'll work closely with our engineering and ML teams to build scalable, reliable, and cost-efficient systems.

A key part of this role is extending our production support coverage beyond UK working hours. We're hiring in Australia or New Zealand to help us work towards 24/7 support for our production customers, so we're looking for someone comfortable taking ownership of live systems, responding to incidents, and making independent technical decisions.

Importantly, this isn't just about keeping our systems running. We want someone who will actively look for ways to improve how we build, deploy, and serve our models, continually experimenting, optimising, and evolving our infrastructure as we scale.

  • Cloud infrastructure: Build, manage, and scale our production infrastructure across GCP and GPU cloud providers using Kubernetes, Docker, and Terraform.

  • Inference optimisation: Continuously improve inference performance, latency, throughput, GPU utilisation, and infrastructure costs through profiling, experimentation, and iteration, rather than simply maintaining the status quo.

  • Platform evolution: Identify bottlenecks and inefficiencies in how we build, deploy, and serve models, and take ownership of implementing improvements.

  • Production reliability: Monitor critical systems, respond to incidents, and help ensure reliable service for our customers outside UK working hours.

Das Kernprodukt unserer Kunden ist über viele Jahre gewachsen, und das sieht man dem Code an. Das Backend läuft auf PHP 8.1 ohne Framework. Im Frontend stehen jQuery und Vanilla-JS neben React, und automatisierte Tests gibt es bisher wenige.

Wohin es gehen soll, ist klar: Das Backend wird schrittweise auf Symfony umgestellt, das Frontend auf React vereinheitlicht. Bis Ende 2027 soll die Migration abgeschlossen sein. Was dafür fehlt, ist kein Plan, sondern Kapazität.

Du triffst eigenständig technische Entscheidungen, bringst dich in Architektur- und Modernisierungsfragen ein und sorgst dafür, dass die Codequalität mit jedem Release besser wird. Dabei bleibt das Produkt im Einsatz: Wartung, Support und neue Features laufen parallel zur Modernisierung.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Legacy-Module bei laufendem Betrieb schrittweise durch Symfony-Services und React-Oberflächen ersetzen

  • Fullstack-Features von der Datenbank bis zum Frontend entwickeln, teils auch als kundenspezifische Erweiterungen

  • Bestehenden Legacy-Code pflegen, debuggen und weiterentwickeln

  • Code-Reviews durchführen und die Testabdeckung ausbauen

Nach 6 Monaten …

… setzt du Features eigenständig um, hast spürbar zur Modernisierung beigetragen, die Codequalität verbessert und bist für die Auszubildenden eine feste Ansprechperson.

Dein Profil

  • Erfahrung: etwa 4–5 Jahre in der professionellen Softwareentwicklung (ein Richtwert, keine harte Grenze)

  • PHP: fundierte Kenntnisse in modernem PHP 8.x mit objektorientierter Architektur, etwa Dependency Injection, Interfaces und SOLID

  • Symfony: nachweisbare Praxiserfahrung mit dem Framework

  • Legacy-Code: Du gehst sicher mit gewachsenen Codebasen um. Du refaktorierst, debuggst und entwickelst weiter, ohne alles neu zu schreiben.

  • JavaScript/React: solide Erfahrung im Frontend, jQuery schreckt dich nicht ab

  • Datenbanken: relationale Datenbanken wie MySQL/MariaDB oder SingleStore und sicherer Umgang mit SQL

  • Tooling: Git und Arbeit mit CI/CD

Roger is the operating system for dental practices. We automate the work dental teams shouldn’t be doing by hand – from treatment plans to patient communication to revenue optimization – and we plug directly into the practice management systems (PMS) that German practices already run on. We’re early, well-funded, and moving fast.

We’re looking for a Senior Product Engineer who wants to own a product area end to end: understand the practice’s problem, decide what to build, ship it, run it, and improve it with real usage data. Not tickets. Outcomes.

We call the role Product Engineer on purpose. You work directly with product, design, and practices, and you’re accountable for whether what you built actually solves the problem – not just for whether the code merged.

What you’ll build
Everyone works across the whole product
column2:
people build deeper expertise in some areas, but who works on what can change quickly. Over a typical quarter you’ll touch things like:
• PMS integrations – connecting Roger to the practice management systems German practices run on, so our workflows sit on top of live practice data instead of beside it
• Treatment plans and cost estimates (HKP) – turning a manual, error-prone paper process into something a practice team gets right the first time
• Patient communication – recalls, reminders, and follow-ups that practices today handle by phone, fax, and sticky note
• Revenue and billing workflows – helping practices bill what they actually did, correctly and on time
• The Roger apps – web and Flutter clients that practice staff use all day, every day

Whatever your area, you’ll own it from the first conversation with a practice to the dashboard that tells you whether it worked.

What we expect
• Own outcomes, not tasks. You define scope, timelines, and success criteria for your area, and you align stakeholders around them
• Make technical decisions and stand behind them. Architecture, trade-offs, what to build versus buy – you decide, document why, and course-correct when the data says so
• Know the system, not just your service. Roger is one product. You keep enough context across PMS integrations, data model, and clients to make decisions that hold up outside your corner
• Raise the bar continuously. Testing, documentation, CI/CD, observability – you leave every area better than you found it
• Shape how we work with AI. Our tooling and practices are still evolving. You contribute to them actively rather than waiting for a playbook
• Enable others. Code reviews, knowledge sharing, pairing – a senior here makes the people around them better

How we work
AI-native engineering, honestly described. Most of us run several coding agents in parallel, all day. Writing code is no longer the bottleneck. Reviewing it, testing it, and deciding what not to ship is. So here’s what that actually means for you:
• You write specs and plans before you prompt. Skipping design thinking is where projects fail – not the AI
• You review agent output with the same rigor as any PR. If you can’t explain what a module does, it doesn’t ship
• You test relentlessly. A solid test suite is how you turn an unreliable agent into a reliable system
• Your fundamentals are strong enough to evaluate, correct, and improve whatever AI produces – architecture, security, performance
• You know the spectrum: when a throwaway prototype is fine and when full engineering discipline applies
• You expect to spend as much time reviewing and validating as writing. If that sounds like a downgrade, this isn’t the right team. If it sounds like leverage, read on

Patient data is not a detail. Roger handles health data (GDPR Art. 9) and sits inside practices bound by professional secrecy (§ 203 StGB). Data minimization, access control, EU processing, and a clear head about what may go to which model provider are part of the engineering bar here – not a compliance checkbox someone else owns.
Small team, short paths. You talk to practices, to product, and to the people who answer the phones for our customers. Decisions get made in a conversation, not a committee.

Who you are
• Senior-level, with significant experience shipping and operating production systems – you’ve been paged for your own code
• A track record of owning projects end to end: from a vague problem statement through delivery to production and iteration
• Used to working cross-functionally with product, design, data, and non-technical stakeholders – and comfortable talking to end users directly
• You think beyond your own code: business context, user needs, and product goals shape what you build
• You take ownership without waiting for instructions, make decisions under ambiguity, and escalate when it matters
• You communicate openly and clearly, in writing and in person, with technical and non-technical people alike
• Our stack is Ruby on Rails, Go, and Dart/Flutter. Deep experience in at least one of these helps

About Niantic Spatial

AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It can't yet reason about real places well enough for robots, field crews and AI agents to rely on it, and closing that gap will change how factories, power grids, cities and defense operations run.

That's one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it's the one we're solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That's why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world's most widely used maps. Now we're building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.

About the Role

The Large Geospatial Model is Niantic Spatial's foundation model of the physical world. It learns from years of real-world captures of millions of places, and people, robots and AI agents use it to find out where they are, what is around them and what has changed. Each step up in scale has given the model capabilities it did not have before. The next problems are some of the hardest in AI: filling in the parts of a place no camera saw while marking what was inferred, measuring what changed between visits, and predicting what will change next.

Customers already use the model in production. Energy companies use it to guide field crews to equipment on large industrial sites, defense partners use it for positioning where GPS is jammed or unavailable, and robotics companies train robots in metric-scale copies of the real sites they will work in.

You will be the first product leader for the model and the data it learns from, reporting to the Chief Product Officer. You decide which capabilities it gains and in what order, the bar each release has to clear, and what data Niantic Spatial collects, licenses or partners for to get there. You set those priorities directly with the Chief Scientist and the London research team who train the model.

If you have shipped a frontier language model, most of the job will be familiar: evals, data mix and release decisions. The job differs in two ways. Every output of this model can be scored against a measured real place, so its evals rest on ground truth. And its data is collected in the physical world, so choosing what to capture next is a product decision with a real cost. Experience in 3D or mapping is welcome but not required.

By the end of your first year, research, engineering and the product leads for industrial, defense, robotics and platform customers work from one model roadmap that you own, each release ships against evals you wrote, and the model's newest capabilities are in customers' hands.

What You'll Do

  • Own the Model Roadmap - Decide the order in which the Large Geospatial Model gains its next capabilities, from filling in unseen parts of a site to measuring and predicting change, based on what industrial, defense, robotics and platform customers will pay for. Turn customer problems into specific research requirements, and bring new research results to the product leads who sell into each market.

  • Set the Release Bar - Define the evals and acceptance criteria for each capability with the Real-World Test Lab, which measures model output against ground truth in real places. Decide whether each release ships or goes back for more data or training.

  • Own the Data Plan - Decide what data Niantic Spatial collects, buys, licenses or gets through partners, and set the product terms of those deals with Legal and Business Development. Set the curation, labeling, consent, privacy and training-rights requirements every dataset has to meet, and keep a record of which data went into each model version.

  • Turn Capabilities into Products - Decide when a new model capability is ready to become something customers buy, what it promises them, and how it reaches them through Niantic Spatial's products and platform.

  • Set the Long-Term Direction - Decide where the model goes over the next several years, as it moves from describing places as they are to tracking how they change and anticipating what comes next, and make the case for the research and data investment that takes.

What You'll Bring

  • 8+ years in product management, including at least three years shipping a large model to users or customers.

  • Experience writing evals for a model and using them to decide when a release was ready.

  • Direct work on training data, such as setting a data mix, running labeling or human-feedback programs, or negotiating data licenses.

  • Enough depth in how large models are trained, post-trained and evaluated that researchers bring you into their technical decisions. Many strong candidates for this role were ML engineers or researchers before they moved into product.

  • Experience setting direction for research and engineering teams that did not report to you.

  • A bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in 3D computer vision, reconstruction, localization, mapping, geospatial data, robotics or autonomous systems.

  • An advanced degree in machine learning, computer vision, robotics, or a related field.

  • Experience with Gaussian splatting, neural fields or visual positioning systems.

  • Experience with government or defense requirements for data provenance and security.

🍊Our mission

Great science regularly stalls in the clinic, not because the science is wrong, but because the company behind it lacks the capital, infrastructure, or focus to take it all the way through. Today’s clinical-stage biopharma model is broken, and as a result promising treatments never reach patients.

Our mission is to fix this: we’re building the next generation of biopharma by in-licensing clinical-stage therapeutic assets and developing them through Lindus Health’s integrated, technology-first clinical trial infrastructure. We’re a new initiative, but we’re building on a proven foundation - the same infrastructure that has delivered 82% of Lindus Health’s sponsor trials on or ahead of timeline, across 40+ completed trials across the US and Europe.

We’re in-licensing 5-7 clinical-stage, typically Phase-2-ready assets, funded directly from Lindus Health’s balance sheet. We’re targeting deal close on our first assets through 2026, with first trials launching in H1 2027.

🍊About the role

The Data Architect owns assigned studies end-to-end, taking full responsibility for both the design of the database on Citrus and the quality of the data it produces, from study planning through database lock. The role designs with the final analysis in mind, writes code where manual review would slow delivery, and designs the edit checks and validation that prevent issues before they make their way downstream. The Data Architect is the technical and data lead for assigned studies and works with Clinical Operations, Biostatistics, Programme Directors, and Product to ensure each study captures the data its scientific objectives require.

One person owns the database from study planning through lock, so the design and the data it produces never drift apart. The role also shapes how data delivery on Citrus develops, identifying where manual work can be automated.

🍊About you

  • You have around 5+ years of experience across clinical data management and/or trial platform design, with hands-on involvement in study setup, data review, and database lock

  • You can design a study's data capture on an EDC platform and define its specification: you understand edit checks and validation, and you can see how a design decision today could become a data quality problem later

  • You work with data programmatically, or are ready to build that skill quickly: Python, R, or SQL are used daily in this role, and you are expected to learn them on the job if you do not already have them

  • You have working knowledge of CDISC standards, particularly CDASH, with SDTM familiarity a plus, and you design with analysis-ready data in mind

  • You have experience with external data transfers and reconciliation

  • You apply AI and automation responsibly to improve the quality and speed of data work in a regulated setting

  • You are passionate about our mission: changing how the healthcare industry operates and how new health treatments are developed

🍊What you’ll focus on

  • Own your assigned studies end-to-end, from defining critical data items and the data management plan through to database lock

  • Own the design of your studies on Citrus, utilizing AI combined with your expert review to translate protocol requirements into a specification and edit check logic that capture clean, analysis-ready data, and sign off that the design meets the protocol before go-live

  • Assess feasibility and flag complexity and risk early, where a design choice could affect data integrity, participant safety or study endpoints

  • Manage the full query lifecycle from generation through resolution, working directly with sites

  • Lead proactive, risk-based data review, automated where possible, to keep key study milestones on track, building repeatable checks rather than one-off reports

  • Use scripting and AI tooling day-to-day to automate data review, flag anomalies, and surface issues earlier, applied responsibly within validation, GCP and 21 CFR Part 11 expectations

  • Own fixes and change requests on your own studies during conduct, assessing their impact and the level of testing and sign-off required

  • Perform ongoing safety data review and facilitate medical coding (MedDRA, WHODrug) with the medical team

  • Build reports using programmatic data access (Python, R, SQL), delivered accurately and on schedule

  • Conduct all activities in line with relevant regulations and Lindus SOPs, keep study documentation to a standard that holds up under audit or inspection, and support auditors and inspectors on your studies where needed

  • Report bugs and usability issues, and feed operational insight back to Product to improve how Citrus supports data delivery

We plan to double the team in 2027. Most companies that grow this fast dilute the talent density that made them good. We won’t.

You’ll hire across GTM: the teams that win our customers and tell the world about Light. One week that might be an enterprise account executive, the next a product marketer or a demand generation lead. You’ll lead Marketing hiring and work alongside our Sales Talent Partner on Sales. It will be fast and at times messy, and you’ll be the person who brings structure to it.

This isn’t a role for someone who wants to sit and screen all day. We want a guardian of the bar: someone who steps back, looks at the whole hiring problem and fixes what’s actually in the way. What You’ll Do

  • Own Marketing hiring end to end, from individual contributors to leadership

  • Work on Sales searches alongside our Sales Talent Partner, including account executives, SDRs and partner sellers

  • Partner with Marketing and Sales leaders from the start: shape the role, challenge the brief, and build the scorecards and calibration that keep the bar high

  • The tools and the time to build. You’ll have Claude, Codex, Lovable, Noon and Ashby from day one, plus a regular team build session to test new workflows. When something works, it becomes how the whole team operates.

  • A strategic role. You’ll help shape GTM hiring plans and market-entry decisions, bringing leadership evidence on where talent sits and what it costs.

  • You switch gears fast. You can move from an enterprise sales search to a product marketing hire in the same afternoon, picking up the language, the market and what good looks like in each.

  • Deep knowledge of the London and European GTM talent market. Without opening LinkedIn, you could tell us which companies build the best Marketing and Sales teams, how they structure comp and OTE, and who’s likely to move.

  • Hands-on experience building with AI to improve recruiting, with examples you can walk us through

Bonus Points

  • Hiring GTM teams for new markets

About us

Plentific is pioneering real-time property operations for real-world impact. Our Software as a Service (SaaS) platform connects owners, operators, service providers and residents. We work with housing associations, local authorities, student housing, later living and build-to-rent operators, across a growing network of 1.7M+ properties and 5,000+ service providers worldwide, reaching 3M+ engaged residents.

Our customers trust us with their residents’ data, their supply chains and their money. This role makes sure that trust is earned every day.

Mission

You'll run Plentific’s compliance programme day to day: KYC, data protection, ISO 27001, business risk and internal audit. You’ll make it practical, evidence-based and quick, using AI tools to do in hours what used to take days.

What you’ll own

  • KYC and due diligence

  • Data protection

  • ISO 27001 ISMS

  • Business risk register

  • Internal audit programme

  • Compliance policies and training

What you’ll do

KYC and due diligence

  • Run KYC checks on customers, suppliers and service providers: identity, ownership, sanctions, PEP and adverse media.

  • Set risk-based rules for when enhanced due diligence applies, and escalate cases that need a decision.

  • Keep KYC records complete and ready for audit or client review.

Data protection

  • Run day-to-day UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018 compliance: records of processing, DPIAs, retention and data subject requests.

  • Review data processing agreements and supplier privacy terms with the legal team.

  • Manage personal data incidents from first report to close, including the decision on whether to notify the ICO within 72 hours.

Information security (ISO 27001)

  • Maintain the ISMS with Information Security Team: Statement of Applicability, risk treatment plan, control owners and evidence, etc.

  • Lead surveillance and recertification audits with our external certification body.

  • Answer security and compliance questionnaires from housing association and local authority clients.

Business risk and internal audit

  • Own the business risk register. Work with risk owners to rate, treat and report risks to the General Counsel and leadership team.

  • Plan and run an annual internal audit programme across information security, data protection and KYC, and track every finding to closure.

  • Report on compliance status and open risks in a format leadership can act on.

Policies, training and AI

  • Keep compliance policies current, short and written so people actually read them.

  • Run awareness training on data protection, information security and KYC.

  • Use AI tools every day to draft policies, review questionnaires and contracts, gather audit evidence and track regulatory change. Automate the repetitive checks.

  • Help shape how Plentific governs its own use of AI.

What you’ll need

  • 3+ years in a compliance, risk or information governance role, ideally in SaaS, fintech or another regulated tech business.

  • Good working knowledge of KYC checks, including sanctions, PEP and beneficial ownership screening, and the tools used to run them.

  • Hands-on experience of UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018: DPIAs, data subject requests, breach handling and supplier due diligence.

  • Experience running or supporting an ISO 27001 ISMS through certification and surveillance audits.

  • A track record of managing a business risk register and conducting internal audits. An ISO 27001 Internal Auditor or Lead Auditor qualification helps.

  • A CIPP/E or CIPM certification is beneficial.

  • AI training credentials are beneficial, such as the IAPP AIGP or an ISO/IEC 42001 Lead Implementer course.

  • You use AI tools daily and can give real examples of how they made your work faster or better.

  • Clear writing, and the confidence to explain a compliance requirement to an engineer, a salesperson or a client.

Nice to have

  • Experience of AI governance, such as the EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001 or the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. Not essential: if you don’t have it yet, you’ll learn it on the job.

You'll join a scale up with ambitious growth plans and the backing to deliver them, in a role where you'll impact the future of housing:

  • 25 days annual holiday

  • Flexible working, including a work abroad scheme

  • Private healthcare for you and immediate family, with discounted gym membership, optical, dental and private GP

  • Enhanced parental leave

  • Life insurance (4x salary)

  • Employee assistance programme

  • Company volunteering day and charity salary sacrifice scheme

  • Referral bonus and charity donation if someone you introduce joins

column3: >Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

>Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

column1: Samsara is a fortress in a volatile market. We are a $1.9B ARR, NYSE-listed powerhouse that sells essential technology to the physical operations powering the global economy. This is a seat built for high performers and incredibly driven individuals who want to accelerate their careers — the bar for entry is high, but those who execute are well rewarded for it.

While the rest of the tech scene is scaling back, our France team continued to perform above 100% last year. We are looking for territory owners who want to manage deal cycles from €20k to €200k, selling a complex suite of 15+ products to 8 different personas, including MDs and Finance Directors. If you want to be pushed to your limit and rewarded with the stability of a market leader, this is the place.
Whilst the role can be worked remotely anywhere in France, there is a need to visit clients in the region as required (typically fortnightly basis).

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

• Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara's top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.

• You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you'll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.

• You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.

• You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven't been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
• You want to be with the best: Samsara's high-performance Sales culture means you'll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.
• Own your destiny: Operate as a pure revenue leader, responsible for 80-90% net-new logo acquisition through self-sourced pipeline.
• Get In Early: The France Mid-Market is a high-achieving segment in the company. The window to build something significant is open right now.
• Sharpen Your Edge: Access elite enablement — Command the Message and MEDDPICC coaching — built to make you a more effective closer.
• Navigate Complexity: Move beyond feature-pushing to sell high-level ROI and safety outcomes to sophisticated economic buyers (MDs and FDs) in the field and the boardroom.
• The Winning DNA: A minimum of 18 months in a full-cycle, outbound-heavy SaaS closing role. You must have a proven history of building your own pipe from scratch.
• Verified Overachievement: A track record of hitting and exceeding quota in a competitive, complex environment. We'll want to see this on your resume.
• Strategic Grit: Experience managing multi-stakeholder deal cycles and technical POCs. We value your ability to hunt more than the brand name on your previous CV.
• Intellectual Curiosity: You are eager to learn the inner workings of diverse industries, from waste management to food distribution, to better align our technology with their operational pain.

• A Repeatable Sales Framework: You don't rely on luck or intuition. You have a structured methodology that delivers success and you understand that consistent, high-quality inputs lead to predictable results.

• A Data-Minded Approach: You are a student of your own funnel. You understand how to structure your activity—prospecting volume, discovery depth, and multi-threading—to ensure a consistent output and forecast accuracy.

• Continuous Process Iteration: You possess a relentless drive for self-improvement. You are someone who actively seeks feedback, iterates on their approach, and understands that evolving your tactics is the only way to stay ahead of the market.

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.
